kcs.label: 主动提供帮助
kcs.description: 主动提出为别人做某事或给别人东西，并接受或婉拒别人的提议。
forms: I'll + base verb (for you).
Shall I + base verb?
Can I help you (with ...)?
Would you like + noun / to + base verb?
Accept: Yes, please. / That's very kind of you. / Thanks a lot.
Decline: No, thanks, I'm fine. / It's OK, I can do it.

examples.en: Your bags look heavy. Shall I help you?
examples.zh: 你的包看起来很重，要我帮忙吗？

examples.en: I'll open the window. It's hot in here.
examples.zh: 我来开窗吧，这里好热。

examples.en: Would you like some more tea? — No, thanks. I'm fine.
examples.zh: 要再来点茶吗？——不用了，谢谢，我够了。

mastery: 能识别 Shall I ...? / I'll ... 是主动提供帮助而不是询问或陈述
能针对图片情境说出合适的提议句
能在角色扮演（招待客人、帮同事）中提出帮助并得体接受或婉拒
commonErrors: 按中文“我帮你”说 *I help you.，应为 I'll help you. 或 Shall I help you?
婉拒时只说 *No.，显得生硬，应说 No, thanks.
boundaries: will 的语法形式见 kt:en-will-future；请求别人帮忙见 kt:en-fn-requests。
服务场合的固定用语（Can I help you? 店员问候）在 A1 服务交际中已作为语块出现。

primitives.binding: Shall I…? / I'll… 提供帮助与接受拒绝回合；检查 *I help you
Can I help? vs Would you like me to…? 礼貌度

kcs.label: 约定见面时间地点
kcs.description: 和别人商量并确定见面的时间、地点和方式，包括询问对方是否有空、提出时间、调整和确认。
forms: Are you free on ...? / What are you doing on ...?
What time shall we meet?
Where shall we meet? — Let's meet outside the ...
How about six o'clock? / Is seven OK for you?
I can't make it at ... Can we make it ... instead?
See you at ... on ... then.

examples.en: Are you free on Thursday? — Sorry, I'm working late. What about Friday?
examples.zh: 你周四有空吗？——抱歉，我要加班。周五怎么样？

examples.en: Let's meet in front of the cinema at quarter to seven.
examples.zh: 我们六点四十五在电影院门口见吧。

examples.en: OK, so we're meeting at the station at ten. See you then!
examples.zh: 好，那我们十点在车站见。到时见！

mastery: 听一段约定对话能记下最终确定的时间和地点
能用 Are you free ...? / What time shall we ...? 等句型询问并提出时间
能在电话或短信角色扮演中协商一次见面（至少一次调整）并最后确认
commonErrors: 时间介词用错：*Let's meet in Friday at the evening.，应为 on Friday evening
问有没有空直译：*Do you have time on Sunday? 可以理解，但 Are you free on Sunday? 更自然
最后不确认，导致信息不清楚
boundaries: 发出与回应邀请本身见 kt:en-fn-invitations；时间介词见 A1 的 kt:en-prepositions-time。
正式会议预约的邮件写作不在 A2 范围。

primitives.binding: 双方日程不同，必须协商出时间地点；检查 on Friday evening（c58）
约见回合含改时间分支

kcs.label: 小组非正式讨论并达成一致
kcs.description: 和朋友或同学进行简短的非正式讨论（如决定去哪里、买什么礼物），提出建议、简单表达同意或不同意，并最终达成一致。
forms: moves: suggest → respond → give simple reason → agree on a decision
Agree: I agree. / Me too. / That's a good idea. / You're right.
Disagree: I'm not sure. / I don't think so. / I don't really like ...
Reason: because it's cheaper / nearer
Decide: So, let's ... / OK, that's decided.
Check others: What do you think? / Is that OK with everyone?

examples.en: What do you think, Mia? — I agree with Sam. The park is nearer.
examples.zh: 米娅，你觉得呢？——我同意萨姆，公园更近。

examples.en: I don't think a book is a good idea. She doesn't read much.
examples.zh: 我觉得送书不太好，她不怎么看书。

examples.en: OK, so we're buying her a scarf. Is that OK with everyone?
examples.zh: 好，那我们就买条围巾送她。大家都同意吗？

mastery: 听一段小组讨论能说出最后的决定和至少一个理由
能在讨论中用固定说法表达同意或不同意并给出简单理由
能在 3–4 人小组中完成一次决策任务，主动询问他人意见并帮助形成结论
commonErrors: 把 agree 当形容词：*I am agree.，应为 I agree.
不同意时过于直接：*No, you are wrong.，A2 可先用 I'm not sure ... 缓和
只说自己的想法，不询问他人，讨论无法达成一致
boundaries: 陈述并论证个人观点在 B1 的 kt:en-fn-opinion 系统展开。
正式会议中的讨论见 B2 的 kt:en-skill-formal-discussion。

primitives.binding: 小组讨论回合：提议、同意、反对、达成一致；检查 I agree 无 be
标出讨论中各发言的功能（c45）

kcs.label: have to / don't have to
kcs.description: have to / has to + 动词原形，表示由规定、制度或客观情况决定的必须做的事；don't have to 表示“不必”，不是“禁止”。
forms: I / You / We / They have to + base verb
He / She has to + base verb
question: Do you have to ...? / Does she have to ...?
negative: don't / doesn't have to + base verb (= not necessary)
past: had to + base verb
pronunciation: have to /ˈhæftə/, has to /ˈhæstə/

examples.en: Nurses often have to work at night.
examples.zh: 护士经常得上夜班。

examples.en: You don't have to bring food. Lunch is free.
examples.zh: 你不用带吃的，午饭免费。

examples.en: Does your sister have to wear a uniform at school?
examples.zh: 你妹妹上学得穿校服吗？

mastery: 能判断 don't have to 句子表示“不必”而非“不许”
能正确构成 have to / has to 的肯定、否定和疑问
能介绍学校、工作或家庭中自己必须做和不必做的事
commonErrors: 第三人称不变形：*She have to go.
否定写成 *I haven't to go.（英式旧用法，现代一般用 don't have to）
把 don't have to 理解为“不准”，与 mustn't 混淆
boundaries: must / mustn't 见 kt:en-must-mustnt；两者差异的系统比较在 B1 的 kt:en-must-vs-have-to。
need to / needn't 见 B1 的 kt:en-need-to。

primitives.binding: have to/has to/don't have to 按人称变；检查 *She have to
have to vs don't have to：必须 vs 不必

kcs.label: must / mustn't
kcs.description: must + 动词原形表示说话人认为必须做（强烈的义务或规定，常见于告示和规则）；mustn't 表示禁止，不许做。
forms: subject + must + base verb (no -s, no to)
subject + mustn't + base verb
pronunciation: mustn't /ˈmʌsnt/ (第一个 t 不发音)
signs and rules: Visitors must sign in.
past obligation uses had to (must has no past form)

examples.en: You must wear a seat belt in the car.
examples.zh: 坐车必须系安全带。

examples.en: You mustn't touch the paintings.
examples.zh: 不许触摸画作。

examples.en: I must call my mum tonight. It's her birthday.
examples.zh: 我今晚一定得给妈妈打电话，今天是她生日。

mastery: 能根据告示或规则判断某事是必须、禁止还是不必
能正确使用 must / mustn't 后的原形动词
能为教室、图书馆等场所写出几条规则
commonErrors: must 后加 to 或第三人称加 -s：*He musts go. / *You must to stop.
用 mustn't 表示“不必”：*You mustn't come tomorrow — it's a holiday.，应为 don't have to
用 must 表示过去：*Yesterday I must work late.，应为 had to
boundaries: must 表示推断（He must be tired）见 B1 的 kt:en-must-cant-deduction。
与 have to 的语用差别见 B1 的 kt:en-must-vs-have-to。

primitives.binding: 义务梯度：must—don't have to—mustn't（必须/不必/禁止）；材料是校规
must 后原形无 -s 无 to

kcs.label: should 给建议
kcs.description: should / shouldn't + 动词原形，表示说话人认为某事是好主意或不是好主意，用于给建议、谈论正确做法。语气比 must 弱。
forms: subject + should + base verb
subject + shouldn't + base verb
question: Should I ...? / What should I do?
I think you should ... / I don't think you should ...
no -s, no to after should

examples.en: You look tired. You should go to bed early tonight.
examples.zh: 你看起来很累，今晚应该早点睡。

examples.en: You shouldn't drink coffee so late.
examples.zh: 你不该这么晚喝咖啡。

examples.en: What should I wear to the interview?
examples.zh: 面试我该穿什么？

mastery: 能区分 should（建议）与 must（强烈必须）在语气上的差异
能正确构成 should 的肯定、否定和疑问句
能针对朋友描述的简单问题给出两条建议
commonErrors: should 后加 to：*You should to see a doctor.
否定位置错误：*I think you should not ... 可以，但更自然的是 I don't think you should ...
第三人称加 -s：*She shoulds rest.
boundaries: 建议功能的其他说法（Why don't you / If I were you）见 kt:en-fn-advice。
ought to 见 B1 的 kt:en-ought-to；should have 见 B1 的 kt:en-past-modals-evaluation。

primitives.binding: 朋友诉苦—给建议回合；检查 should 后无 to
could—should—must 建议强度定位（c17）

kcs.label: 说明规则、义务与必要
kcs.description: 说明在某地或某事中必须做、不许做和不必做的事，例如介绍学校规定、工作要求、旅行签证手续，并询问规则。
forms: You have to ... / You must ...
You mustn't ... / You can't ... (prohibition)
You don't have to ... (not necessary)
Do I have to ...? / Is it OK to ...?
It's necessary to ... / You need to ... (chunk)
You're (not) allowed to ...

examples.en: At our gym, you have to show your card, but you don't have to book.
examples.zh: 我们健身房要出示会员卡，但不用预约。

examples.en: Do I have to pay for the bags? — Yes, they're 20 cents each.
examples.zh: 袋子要付钱吗？——要，每个两毛。

examples.en: You can't smoke here, and you mustn't leave bags by the door.
examples.zh: 这里不能吸烟，也不许把包放在门口。

mastery: 读一份简单规定后能分类：必须、禁止、不必
能根据情境选择 have to / must / mustn't / don't have to
能向新同学或新同事口头介绍一个地方的主要规定，并回答对方关于规则的问题
commonErrors: 把“不必”说成“禁止”：*You mustn't pay. It's free.
把建议说成规则：*You must try the noodles here.（推荐时语气过强，可用 should）
boundaries: 单个情态动词的形式见 kt:en-have-to、kt:en-must-mustnt。
给个人建议而非说明规则见 kt:en-fn-advice。

primitives.binding: 必须/不必/禁止梯度定位；检查 mustn't 不当“不必”
在规则告示中找出必须/禁止/免费的条目

kcs.label: 提出建议与忠告
kcs.description: 针对别人遇到的问题给出建议，或请别人给自己建议，并对建议作出回应。
forms: You should / shouldn't ...
I think you should ...
Why don't you ...?
Have you tried + -ing?
Asking: What should I do? / Can you give me some advice?
Responses: That's a good idea. / Thanks, I'll try that.

examples.en: I can't sleep at night. — Why don't you turn off your phone an hour before bed?
examples.zh: 我晚上睡不着。——你为什么不在睡前一小时关掉手机呢？

examples.en: My English isn't improving. What should I do?
examples.zh: 我的英语没进步，我该怎么办？

examples.en: I think you should talk to your teacher about it.
examples.zh: 我觉得你应该和老师谈谈这件事。

mastery: 能识别对话中的求助和建议，并判断建议是否被接受
能对常见问题（生病、学习、失眠）给出至少两种不同句型的建议
能写一条简短回复，针对朋友留言中的问题给出建议
commonErrors: advice 当可数名词：*Can you give me an advice? / *some advices，应为 some advice / a piece of advice
Why don't you 后用 to：*Why don't you to rest?
boundaries: If I were you ... 需要第二条件句，见 B1 的 kt:en-second-conditional。
共同行动的提议（Let's ...）见 kt:en-fn-suggestions。

primitives.binding: 求建议—给建议—回应回合；检查 advice 不可数
建议强度梯度 You should/You might want to（c17）

kcs.label: 提出请求与回应
kcs.description: 请别人做某事或请求获得某物、许可，并对别人的请求表示同意或拒绝。A2 要求能根据对象调整礼貌程度。
forms: Can you + base verb ...?
Could you + base verb ..., please?
Can I / Could I + base verb ...?
Can I have ..., please?
Agree: Sure. / Of course. / No problem.
Refuse: Sorry, I can't. I'm ... / I'm afraid ...

examples.en: Could you send me the photos, please? — Sure, I'll do it tonight.
examples.zh: 你能把照片发给我吗？——当然，我今晚发。

examples.en: Can I borrow your pen for a minute?
examples.zh: 能借你的笔用一下吗？

examples.en: Sorry, I can't lend you my car. I need it today.
examples.zh: 抱歉，我不能把车借给你，我今天要用。

mastery: 能判断请求是请对方做事（Could you）还是请求许可（Could I）
能对朋友和陌生人分别使用 Can you / Could you ... please
能在商店、学校、邻里等情境的角色扮演中提出请求并得体回应别人的请求
commonErrors: 受中文“请帮我……”影响用祈使句：*Please give me your pen.（对陌生人显得生硬）
Could I 与 Could you 混用：*Could you borrow me your pen? 应为 Could you lend me / Could I borrow
boundaries: 更间接、更礼貌的软化方式见 kt:en-soc-softening。
can / could 的形式见 A1 的 kt:en-can-could-requests。

primitives.binding: Please give me vs Could you…? vs Would you mind…? 按对象调（c17）
请求—同意/拒绝回合

kcs.label: 用间接方式让请求更礼貌
kcs.description: 英语中请求越间接通常越礼貌：用问句代替命令、加 please、用 could / would、先铺垫理由或说 I was wondering 等，使对方容易拒绝。适合对陌生人、上级或请求负担较大时。
forms: Imperative → question: Close the door. → Could you close the door?
Would you mind + -ing ...?
Do you think you could ...?
I was wondering if you could ...
Sorry to bother you, but ...
softeners: just, a minute, a bit — Could I just ask a quick question?

examples.en: Sorry to bother you, but could you tell me where the toilets are?
examples.zh: 不好意思打扰一下，请问洗手间在哪里？

examples.en: Would you mind opening the window? — No, not at all.
examples.zh: 你介意打开窗户吗？——不介意。

examples.en: I was wondering if you could help me with my CV.
examples.zh: 不知道你能不能帮我看看简历。

mastery: 能把几种请求按礼貌程度排序
能把一个直接的祈使句改写成两种更礼貌的请求
能根据对象（朋友、老师、陌生人）和请求大小选择合适的礼貌程度
commonErrors: 回答 Would you mind ...? 时说 *Yes, sure.（字面意思是“介意”），同意时应说 No, not at all. / Of course not.
Would you mind 后用原形：*Would you mind open the door?
对朋友小事也用过度正式的说法，显得疏远
boundaries: 基本请求形式见 kt:en-fn-requests；问路等间接疑问句（Can you tell me where ... is?）的语序规则见 B1 的 kt:en-embedded-questions。
I was wondering if 在 A2 作为整体语块学习，不要求分析时态。

primitives.binding: 请求的直接度梯度：I was wondering if…、Would you mind…（c17）；检查答 No, not at all
答 *Yes, sure 回应 Would you mind 造成误会，判读改写

kcs.label: may / might 表达可能
kcs.description: may / might + 动词原形，表示某事有可能发生或有可能是真的，但不确定。A2 阶段两者基本可互换，might 在口语中略常见、略不确定。
forms: subject + may / might + base verb
negative: may not / might not (mightn't 较少)
I might go to the party, but I'm not sure.
It may rain later.
questions with might are rare; use Do you think ...? instead

examples.en: Take an umbrella. It might rain this afternoon.
examples.zh: 带把伞吧，今天下午可能会下雨。

examples.en: I may not finish the report today.
examples.zh: 我今天可能完不成报告。

examples.en: We might go to the beach on Sunday, if the weather is good.
examples.zh: 周日天气好的话我们可能去海边。

mastery: 能区分 will（确定）与 may / might（不确定）表达的把握程度
能正确构成肯定与否定句（may not 不缩写为 *mayn't）
能用 might 谈论自己不确定的周末计划或天气
commonErrors: may / might 后加 to 或变形：*She might comes. / *It may to rain.
把 may be（情态 + be）和 maybe（副词）混写：*Maybe it rain. / *It maybe true.
boundaries: May I ...? 表示请求许可属于请求功能，不在本知识点内。
确定度的系统比较见 B1 的 kt:en-certainty-scale。

primitives.binding: will/may/might 按把握程度放上梯度；检查 *might comes
情态后原形，无 to 无 -s

kcs.label: possibly / probably / perhaps
kcs.description: 用副词 perhaps、maybe、possibly、probably 表达说话人对事情的把握程度：probably 把握较大，perhaps / maybe / possibly 把握较小。
forms: probably: after will / be, before won't — He'll probably come. / He probably won't come.
perhaps / maybe: usually at the start — Maybe she's ill.
possibly: It's possibly the best café in town.
short answers: Probably. / Maybe. / Possibly. / Probably not.
certainty scale: definitely > probably > perhaps / maybe / possibly

examples.en: Where's Leo? — Maybe he's still at work.
examples.zh: 利奥在哪？——也许他还在上班。

examples.en: We'll probably arrive around eight.
examples.zh: 我们大概八点左右到。

examples.en: Are you coming tomorrow? — Probably not. I've got a cold.
examples.zh: 你明天来吗？——可能不来了，我感冒了。

mastery: 能根据副词判断说话人把握程度的高低
能把 probably 放在 will 之后、won't 之前的正确位置
回答关于将来或不确定情况的问题时能用这些副词给出有把握程度的回答
commonErrors: probably 位置错误：*He probably will not come. 可接受但不常见；*He won't probably come. 错
把 maybe 当动词修饰词放在句中：*He maybe is at home.，应为 Maybe he's at home. 或 He may be at home.
boundaries: 情态动词 may / might 表达可能见 kt:en-may-might。
will / probably / may / might 的综合确定度梯度见 B1 的 kt:en-certainty-scale。

primitives.binding: probably 在 will 后、won't 前；挪动看位置
probably/possibly/perhaps 按确定度选

kcs.label: 零条件句：规律
kcs.description: If / When + 一般现在时，主句也用一般现在时，表示总是成立的规律、事实或习惯：条件一出现，结果就出现。
forms: If + present simple, present simple
When + present simple, present simple (≈ if for general truths)
If you heat ice, it melts.
If I'm tired, I go to bed early.
If + present, imperative: If you feel sick, tell the teacher.

examples.en: If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.
examples.zh: 蓝色和黄色混合就会变成绿色。

examples.en: If my sister doesn't sleep enough, she gets angry easily.
examples.zh: 我妹妹要是睡不够，就容易发脾气。

examples.en: When it snows, the buses are always late.
examples.zh: 一下雪，公交总是晚点。

mastery: 能判断一个 if 句是在说一般规律还是某一次可能的情况
能用一般现在时完成零条件句的两个部分
能用零条件句说明自己生活中的习惯或简单科学事实
commonErrors: 受中文“如果……就……”影响加 so 或 then 连接：*If you heat water, so it boils.
主语第三人称漏 -s：*If water get hot, it boil.
boundaries: 针对具体将来情况的条件用第一条件句，见 kt:en-first-conditional。
与现实相反的假设见 B1 的 kt:en-second-conditional。

primitives.binding: 条件与结果接成 If…,…；检查不加 so/then 叠用
If 句判断是普遍规律还是具体将来

kcs.label: 第一条件句：开放的未来条件
kcs.description: If + 一般现在时，主句用 will（或 may / can / 祈使句），表示将来某个有可能发生的条件及其结果。if 从句虽说将来，却用一般现在时。
forms: If + present simple, will / won't + base verb
will + base verb + if + present simple (no comma)
If + present, might / can + base verb
If + present, imperative: If you see Tom, tell him to call me.
unless = if ... not (recognition only)

examples.en: If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay at home.
examples.zh: 如果明天下雨，我们就待在家里。

examples.en: You'll miss the bus if you don't hurry.
examples.zh: 你不快点就赶不上公交了。

examples.en: If I have time this weekend, I might visit you.
examples.zh: 这周末要是有空，我可能去看你。

mastery: 能分辨条件部分与结果部分，并说出 if 从句用一般现在时
能完成或改写第一条件句，正确处理逗号和时态
能用第一条件句谈论计划的不同可能（天气、考试、预算）或提出警告
commonErrors: if 从句也用 will：*If it will rain, we will stay home.
主句漏 will：*If you study hard, you pass the exam.（在零条件句中成立，但表达对具体将来的预测时应加 will）
加 so：*If I have time, so I will call you.
boundaries: 一般规律用零条件句，见 kt:en-zero-conditional；when 表示将来必然发生的时间也用一般现在时，见 kt:en-before-after。
unless 的系统使用在 B1 扩展。

primitives.binding: if 从句用一般现在、主句 will；检查 *If it will rain

kcs.label: 动名词作名词性成分
kcs.description: 动词加 -ing 当名词用（动名词），可作主语、宾语或介词宾语，表示一种活动。例如 Swimming is fun、I'm good at drawing。
forms: subject: Cooking is my hobby.
after verbs: enjoy, finish, mind, stop, practise + -ing
after like / love / hate / prefer + -ing
after prepositions: good at, interested in, afraid of, before / after + -ing
go + -ing for activities: go shopping, go swimming
negative: not + -ing

examples.en: Learning a new language takes time.
examples.zh: 学一门新语言需要时间。

examples.en: I'm not very good at remembering names.
examples.zh: 我不太擅长记人名。

examples.en: Have you finished cleaning your room?
examples.zh: 你打扫完房间了吗？

mastery: 能在句中识别 -ing 作名词（动名词）还是进行时的一部分
能在 enjoy、finish、介词等后面正确使用 -ing
能用动名词作主语谈论爱好和活动（Reading helps me relax）
commonErrors: 受中文无形态变化影响用原形作主语：*Swim is good for you.
介词后用原形或不定式：*I'm interested in learn Spanish. / *She's good at to sing.
enjoy 后接不定式：*I enjoy to read.
boundaries: 哪些动词后接 to 不定式见 kt:en-verb-to-infinitive；like + -ing 的语块已在 A1 的 kt:en-like-ing。
动名词与不定式意义不同的动词（stop, remember, try）在 B1 再处理。

primitives.binding: Swimming is fun 中 -ing 作主语，判断哪个是动作名称
动词→动名词作主语/宾语/介词后，检查 *Swim is good

kcs.label: 动词 + to 不定式
kcs.description: 某些动词后面接 to + 动词原形作宾语，多与意愿、计划、决定有关（want, hope, decide, plan）。是否接 to 不定式由前面的动词决定，需要按动词记忆。
forms: want / would like + to + base verb
hope / plan / decide / need / try / learn / forget / agree + to + base verb
negative: decide not to + base verb
would like / want + object + to: I want you to come.
contrast: enjoy / finish / mind + -ing
like / love / hate + -ing or to (little difference at A2)

examples.en: We've decided to move to a bigger flat.
examples.zh: 我们决定搬到大一点的公寓。

examples.en: Don't forget to lock the door.
examples.zh: 别忘了锁门。

examples.en: I'm learning to drive, but I enjoy taking the bus.
examples.zh: 我在学开车，不过我喜欢坐公交。

mastery: 能把常见动词分成接 to 不定式和接 -ing 两组
能在句中为给定动词选择 to 不定式或 -ing
能用 want / hope / plan / decide 谈论自己今年的打算
commonErrors: 漏掉 to：*I want go home. / *She decided buy it.
want 后用 that 从句：*I want that you come.，应为 I want you to come.
to 后用变化形式：*I hope to seeing you.
boundaries: to 不定式表示目的（I went out to buy milk）见 kt:en-infinitive-purpose。
接两种形式且意义不同的动词（stop to do / stop doing）在 B1 处理。

primitives.binding: want/decide/hope + to do 用例裁判；检查 *I want go
接 to do 的动词表先回想再揭示

kcs.label: to 不定式表目的
kcs.description: 用 to + 动词原形说明做某事的目的，回答 Why?，相当于中文“为了……”“去……”。
forms: verb + (object) + to + base verb: I went to the shop to buy bread.
answer to Why?: To get some exercise.
I'm saving money to buy a bike.
negative purpose (A2 recognition): so that I don't ... / in order not to
contrast: for + noun (for a coffee), not for + verb

examples.en: I called the hotel to ask about parking.
examples.zh: 我打电话给酒店询问停车的事。

examples.en: Why are you learning English? — To get a better job.
examples.zh: 你为什么学英语？——为了找份更好的工作。

examples.en: She went out for a coffee and to meet a friend.
examples.zh: 她出去喝咖啡，也顺便见个朋友。

mastery: 能在句中找出目的部分，并回答 Why? 问题
能把两个句子合并成一个带 to 不定式目的的句子
能说明自己做几件日常事情的目的（去某地、学某技能）
commonErrors: 用 for + 动词表目的：*I came here for study English. / *for to buy，应为 to study / to buy
受中文“为了”影响多加 for：*for to learn
boundaries: 动词后作宾语的 to 不定式（want to go）见 kt:en-verb-to-infinitive。
so that / in order to 的完整目的从句在 B1 扩展。

primitives.binding: to + V 表目的 vs for + 名词；检查 *for study English
动作+目的两句接成一句

kcs.label: much / many 与数量提问
kcs.description: many 用于可数名词复数，much 用于不可数名词，常用于否定句和疑问句；How many / How much 用来问数量，How much 也问价格。肯定句中更常用 a lot of。
forms: How many + plural noun ...?
How much + uncountable noun ...?
How much is / are ...? (price)
not many + plural / not much + uncountable
a lot of / lots of in positive sentences
too many / too much

examples.en: How many people are coming to the party?
examples.zh: 有多少人来参加聚会？

examples.en: We haven't got much time. Let's take a taxi.
examples.zh: 我们时间不多了，打车吧。

examples.en: There aren't many shops in my village, but there's a lot of green space.
examples.zh: 我们村商店不多，但绿地很多。

mastery: 能根据名词可数与否选择 much 或 many
能用 How much / How many 提问数量和价格，并给出回答
能在购物、准备聚会等情境中询问和说明所需数量
commonErrors: 不可数名词用 many：*How many money / homework / information ...?
肯定句用 much 显得不自然：*I have much friends / *I drink much water.（应为 a lot of）
How many 后用单数：*How many apple do you want?
boundaries: 可数与不可数的判断见 A1 的 kt:en-countability。
few / little 等更多数量词见 kt:en-determiners-wider。

primitives.binding: much/many 按名词可数性归类；检查 *How many money/homework
How much/many…? 问出购物清单数量

kcs.label: all / none / enough / (a) few / (a) little
kcs.description: 表示范围和数量的一组限定词：all（全部）、none / not any（没有）、enough（足够）、a few / a little（有一些）、few / little（几乎没有）。a few / few 用于可数，a little / little 用于不可数。
forms: all + plural / uncountable: All students ... / all the money
none of + the / my + noun; none as pronoun
not any + noun = no + noun
enough + noun / adjective + enough: enough chairs / big enough
a few + plural (some) / few + plural (not many)
a little + uncountable (some) / little + uncountable (not much)

examples.en: There's a little milk left, but we haven't got enough for a cake.
examples.zh: 还剩一点牛奶，但不够做蛋糕。

examples.en: I've invited a few friends for dinner.
examples.zh: 我请了几个朋友来吃晚饭。

examples.en: None of my classmates live near the school.
examples.zh: 我的同学没有一个住在学校附近。

mastery: 能根据名词可数与否选择 a few 或 a little
能区分 a few（有一些，正面）与 few（几乎没有，负面）的含义
能用 enough / not enough / all / none 描述一次活动的准备情况
commonErrors: a few / a little 与名词错配：*a little apples / *a few water
enough 与形容词语序错误：*enough big，应为 big enough
none 与否定词重复：*None of them didn't come.
boundaries: most / both / either / neither 等见 B1 的 kt:en-determiners-broad。
too + 形容词与 enough 的对比见 B1 的 kt:en-too-enough。

primitives.binding: a few/a little/enough 按可数性配名词；检查 *a little apples
few vs a few 判断说话人觉得多还是少

kcs.label: the 与零冠词
kcs.description: the 用于说话双方都知道是哪一个的人或事物（上文提过、独一无二、语境明确）；泛指一类事物时，复数和不可数名词通常不用冠词（零冠词），如 I like music。
forms: the + second mention: a cat ... the cat
the + unique: the sun, the internet, the station (in our town)
the + superlatives / ordinals: the best, the first
zero article for general plurals / uncountables: Dogs are friendly. / Coffee is expensive.
zero article in fixed phrases: at home, go to school, by bus, have breakfast
the + specific uncountable: The coffee in this café is good.

examples.en: I love music, but I don't like the music in this shop.
examples.zh: 我喜欢音乐，但不喜欢这家店放的音乐。

examples.en: We bought a table and two chairs. The table was cheap.
examples.zh: 我们买了一张桌子和两把椅子。桌子很便宜。

examples.en: Children usually go to school by bus here.
examples.zh: 这里的孩子一般坐公交上学。

mastery: 能解释具体句子中为什么用 the 或不用冠词（特指 / 泛指）
能在短文填空中正确选择 a / an / the / 零冠词
写作和口语中常用固定短语（at home, by bus, go to bed）的冠词基本正确
commonErrors: 汉语无冠词，泛指时多加 the：*The life is beautiful. / *I like the sports.
特指时漏 the：*Can you close door?
固定短语加冠词：*go to the bed / *by a bus
boundaries: 不定冠词 a / an 见 A1 的 kt:en-articles-a-an。
抽象名词和机构名称（the hospital / in hospital）的冠词问题见 B2 的 kt:en-articles-abstract。

primitives.binding: 泛指零冠词 vs 特指 the；检查 *The life is beautiful（c15）
I like the sports 等用例裁判

kcs.label: fewer 与 less 的比较
kcs.description: 比较数量多少时，可数名词复数用 fewer / more，不可数名词用 less / more。less 也可用作形容词和副词比较（less expensive）。
forms: fewer + plural noun (+ than): fewer cars
less + uncountable noun (+ than): less sugar
more + plural / uncountable
less + adjective: less expensive, less busy
in informal speech less + plural is common but often seen as incorrect in writing

examples.en: There are fewer students in the class this year.
examples.zh: 今年班上的学生少了。

examples.en: I'm trying to eat less sugar and drink more water.
examples.zh: 我在努力少吃糖、多喝水。

examples.en: The train is less comfortable than the plane, but it's cheaper.
examples.zh: 火车没有飞机舒服，但更便宜。

mastery: 能根据名词可数与否选择 fewer 或 less
能用 more / fewer / less ... than 比较两个地方或两种生活方式
能在描述变化（今年和去年、城市和乡村）时准确使用这些比较词
commonErrors: 可数名词用 less：*less people / *less cars（口语常见，但正式书面视为错误）
less 与 -er 叠加：*less cheaper
boundaries: 形容词比较级本身见 A1 的 kt:en-comparatives。
the least / the fewest 等最高级用法在 B1 处理。

primitives.binding: fewer+可数 vs less+不可数；标注 less people 口语可见、正式书面不宜
less people 口语 vs 书面裁判

kcs.label: quite / so / a bit
kcs.term: Basic intensifiers: quite, so, a bit
kcs.description: 在 very / really 之外，用 quite（相当）、so（非常，带感叹语气）、a bit（有点，多用于负面）调节形容词的程度，使描述更准确、更自然。
forms: quite + adjective: quite good, quite expensive
quite a / an + adjective + noun: quite a long way
so + adjective (no noun after): It's so cold!
so + adjective + that ... (recognition)
a bit + adjective (often negative): a bit tired, a bit noisy
a bit + comparative: a bit cheaper

examples.en: The hotel was quite nice, but the room was a bit small.
examples.zh: 酒店还挺不错，就是房间有点小。

examples.en: Thank you so much! You're so kind.
examples.zh: 太感谢了！你人真好。

examples.en: Can we walk a bit slower? I'm a bit tired.
examples.zh: 我们能走慢一点吗？我有点累。

mastery: 能按程度强弱排列 a bit / quite / very / so
能为形容词选择合适的程度词，并注意 a bit 多用于不太好的特征
描述地点、天气、食物时能用这些词表达细微的评价
commonErrors: a bit 直接加名词：*a bit problem，应为 a bit of a problem 或 a small problem
so 直接修饰带名词的形容词：*It's so nice day.，应为 such a nice day 或 The day is so nice
a bit 用于正面评价显得奇怪：*She's a bit beautiful.
boundaries: very / really 见 A1 的 kt:en-basic-intensifiers。
extremely、much too 等更强的程度词见 B1 的 kt:en-wide-intensifiers；quite 在英美语中的程度差异不在 A2 处理。

primitives.binding: a bit—quite—so 强度定位，注意英式 quite；检查 *a bit problem
a bit of a problem 用例裁判

kcs.label: 教育
kcs.description: 谈论学校生活、科目、课程、考试和学习经历的话题词汇与常用说法，用于自我介绍、谈论过去和计划未来的学习。
forms: primary school / secondary school / university / college
subject, maths, science, history, geography, PE
timetable, homework, exam / test, mark / grade
classmate, teacher, head teacher, student
pass / fail an exam, take an exam
study, learn, revise, graduate
course, lesson, term, degree
My favourite subject is ... / I'm good at ...

examples.en: I passed my maths exam, but I failed history.
examples.zh: 我数学考试过了，但历史没及格。

examples.en: When I was at primary school, my favourite subject was art.
examples.zh: 我上小学时最喜欢的科目是美术。

examples.en: I'm doing an online course in photography this term.
examples.zh: 这学期我在上一门线上摄影课。

mastery: 能把科目、学校类型和学习活动词汇与图片或定义配对
能区分 learn / study / teach、pass / fail / take an exam 的基本用法
能介绍自己过去或现在的学校生活：科目、喜好、考试和计划
commonErrors: take an exam 与 pass 混淆：中文“考试”直译 *I will pass an exam tomorrow.（意思变成“我明天会及格”）
learn 与 study 混用：*I study how to swim.，学会技能多用 learn
homework 当可数名词：*many homeworks

kcs.label: 常见短语动词
kcs.description: 由动词加小品词（up, on, off, out 等）构成的常用短语动词，意义常常不能从字面推出，是日常口语的高频表达。A2 先作为整体语块学习。
forms: get up
wake up
put on
take off
turn on / turn off
look for
look after
give up
come back
go out
sit down
stand up
find out
get on / get off (a bus)
fill in (a form)
pick up
throw away
try on

examples.en: Can you turn off the lights when you go out?
examples.zh: 你出门的时候能把灯关了吗？

examples.en: I'm looking for my keys. Have you seen them?
examples.zh: 我在找钥匙，你看到了吗？

examples.en: Try this jacket on. I think it's your size.
examples.zh: 试试这件外套，我觉得是你的尺码。

mastery: 能把常见短语动词与其意思或图片配对
能在情境中选择正确的短语动词（put on / take off，get on / get off）
描述日常作息和家务时能自然使用 5 个以上短语动词
commonErrors: 按中文逐字理解：look after（照顾）误解为“看后面”
代词宾语放在小品词后：*Turn off it.，应为 Turn it off.
漏掉小品词：*Please fill this form.，应为 fill in this form

primitives.binding: look after/look for/look up 判断意思，不按字面拆
从对话中采集短语动词收进语块本（c02）

kcs.label: that 从句（I think that…）
kcs.description: 在 think、know、say、hope、be sure 等动词后接一个完整句子作宾语，引导词 that 在口语中常省略。用于表达看法、所知道的事和转述别人的话。
forms: I think (that) + clause
I don't think (that) + clause (否定前移)
I know / hope / believe (that) + clause
He says (that) + clause
I'm sure (that) + clause
Do you think (that) ...?

examples.en: I think the shop closes at six.
examples.zh: 我觉得那家店六点关门。

examples.en: I don't think this is a good idea.
examples.zh: 我觉得这不是个好主意。

examples.en: My teacher says that we need to practise every day.
examples.zh: 老师说我们需要每天练习。

mastery: 能识别句中 that 从句的范围，并知道 that 可省略
能使用 I don't think + 肯定从句表达否定看法
能在讨论中用 I think / I'm sure / I hope 表达自己的看法和期望
commonErrors: 受中文“我觉得他不会来”影响把否定放在从句：I think he won't come. 语法正确，但英语更常说 I don't think he'll come.
从句中漏主语或动词：*I think is a good idea.
把 that 从句当疑问句：*I know where is the station.（属间接疑问，语序应为 where the station is）
boundaries: 转述他人话语的时态变化见 B1 的 kt:en-reported-statements；wh- 间接疑问见 B1 的 kt:en-embedded-questions。
关系从句中的 that（the book that I read）不属于本知识点。

primitives.binding: I don't think he'll come vs I think he won't 否定前移偏好
想法+内容用 that 接成一句

kcs.label: 读懂指示、说明与条件
kcs.description: 读懂日常生活中的指示性文本：路线说明、简单的使用说明、操作步骤、规则与条件（如退货条件、优惠条款、警示），并据此采取正确行动。
forms: text types: directions, product / machine instructions, recipes, rules and conditions, warnings
imperatives and numbered steps: 1. Press ... 2. Wait ...
sequence words: first, then, when, until
conditions: If ..., ... / Only ... / You must ... / Do not ...
warning words: Caution, Warning, Keep away from ..., Do not ...
key words: free, valid, refund, receipt, available

examples.en: To get a refund, bring the item back within 14 days with your receipt.
examples.zh: 如需退款，请在 14 天内持收据退回商品。

examples.en: Press the green button and wait until the light goes off.
examples.zh: 按绿色按钮，等指示灯熄灭。

examples.en: Warning: Do not leave children alone near the pool.
examples.zh: 警告：不要让儿童单独在泳池附近。

mastery: 读一份短说明能把步骤图片排成正确顺序
能根据条件文本判断某个具体情况是否符合要求（如能否退货）
能按照一份真实或改编的说明完成一项任务（操作机器、找到地点）
commonErrors: 忽略条件词（only, within, unless, if），只看关键词就行动
把 Do not ... 前的否定看漏，误解为允许
boundaries: A1 的标识与告示见 kt:en-skill-read-signs；当面听指令见 kt:en-skill-listen-directions。
合同、官方指南等较长的规范文本见 B2 的 kt:en-skill-read-documents。

primitives.binding: 在说明书、作业要求中找出条件词 only/within/unless 所限定的一条
含 unless/only 的指令判断是否该做

kcs.label: 读懂私人信件、简短正式信件与留言
kcs.description: 读懂朋友的私人信件、电子邮件和留言，以及简单的事务性信件（如确认、通知），找出写信人讲了什么事、有什么计划、需要读者做什么。
forms: text types: personal emails, letters, text messages, notes; short formal letters (confirmation, notice)
openings: Hi / Dear ..., How are you?
news in past tense: Last week I ...
plans: I'm going to ... / We're visiting ...
requests: Can you ...? / Please let me know ...
closings: See you soon / Best wishes / Yours sincerely

examples.en: Thanks for your email. We're having a barbecue on Sunday. Can you bring some drinks?
examples.zh: 谢谢你的邮件。我们周日要搞烧烤，你能带点饮料吗？

examples.en: Dear Ms Chen, this is to confirm your appointment on 3 May at 10 a.m.
examples.zh: 陈女士您好，特此确认您 5 月 3 日上午 10 点的预约。

mastery: 能找出信件的写信目的（分享消息、邀请、请求、确认）
能回答关于信中事件、时间和计划的具体问题
能根据信件内容判断自己需要做什么回应，并列出要点
commonErrors: 只读字面，忽略信中隐含的请求（Let me know if ... 表示需要回复）
把非正式信件和正式信件的开头结尾混用
boundaries: 写便条和短消息见 A1 的 kt:en-skill-write-messages；写正式信件见 B2 的 kt:en-skill-write-formal-correspondence。
只要求读懂简短、话题熟悉的正式信件，不包括复杂的商务或法律信函。

primitives.binding: 读信辨隐含请求 Let me know if… 需回复；材料是私人与简短正式信
字面陈述背后的请求
在邮件中找时间地点要求

kcs.label: 略读与扫读
kcs.description: 两种快速阅读策略：略读（skim）快速浏览标题、首句和图片，判断文本讲什么、是否与自己相关；扫读（scan）带着问题快速寻找特定信息，如时间、价格、名字。
forms: skim: read title, headings, first lines, pictures to get the topic / text type
scan: decide what you need (a number, a name, a time), then look only for it
use layout clues: bold words, lists, tables, numbers
do not read every word
texts: timetables, websites, leaflets, menus, adverts, short articles

examples.en: Look at these three adverts. Which one is about a language course?
examples.zh: 看这三则广告，哪一则是关于语言课程的？（略读）

examples.en: Find the time of the last bus on Sunday.
examples.zh: 找出周日末班车的时间。（扫读）

mastery: 能在限时内判断几篇短文本分别是什么类型、关于什么主题
能在时刻表、网页或传单中快速找到指定信息
能根据任务目的自己选择略读还是扫读，而不是逐词阅读
commonErrors: 逐词逐句翻译，导致时间不够
扫读时找到相似的词就作答，没有核对上下文（如找到 Saturday 的时间当作 Sunday）
boundaries: 抓住长文主旨与要点见 B1 的 kt:en-str-key-points；推测生词见 B1 的 kt:en-str-guess-from-context。
本知识点是策略，不涉及具体文本类型的理解深度。

primitives.binding: 限时在长文中找特定信息（扫读）；检查不逐词翻译
略读后给每段贴主旨标签（c25）

kcs.label: 连续独白：描述与介绍计划
kcs.description: 不依赖对方提问，连续说一小段话（约 1–2 分钟）描述人、地点、日常生活或计划，用简单连接词把句子连起来。
forms: topics: my family, my home, my town, my daily routine, my plans
opening: I'd like to tell you about ...
linking: and, but, because, also, then
description structures: There is / are, It's got, He's ...
closing: That's all about ... / So that's my ...
about 8–12 connected sentences

examples.en: I'd like to tell you about my grandmother. She's seventy but she's very active. She walks every morning and she also teaches dancing.
examples.zh: 我想讲讲我奶奶。她七十岁了，但非常活跃。她每天早上散步，还教跳舞。

examples.en: So that's my town. It's not exciting, but I love it because it's quiet and green.
examples.zh: 这就是我的小镇。它不算热闹，但我很喜欢，因为安静又绿意盎然。

mastery: 能根据一张提示卡列出描述要点
能用连接词把 6–8 句话连成一段描述
能在准备 1–2 分钟后连续描述一个熟悉的人、地点或计划，听者能复述主要内容
commonErrors: 只说孤立的短句，中间停顿很长，没有连接
频繁使用中文填充词（“那个”“就是”）代替英语的 well / and / so
boundaries: 有准备的正式陈述并回答提问见 B2 的 kt:en-skill-presentation。
来源单元也包含“介绍计划”的独白，本知识点以描述为主、计划为辅。

primitives.binding: 从一句计划扩成连贯独白，每步加连接（c38）
录独白自转写，看停顿与连接（c55）

kcs.label: 用固定说法请求澄清
kcs.term: Asking for clarification with stock phrases
kcs.description: 在交谈中没听懂某个关键词或短语时，用固定说法请对方解释、拼写或换个说法，而不是假装听懂或中断交流。
forms: Sorry, what does ... mean?
What do you mean by ...?
Sorry, did you say ... or ...?
Can you spell that, please?
Can you say that in a different way?
Sorry, I don't understand the word ...

examples.en: Sorry, what does 'refund' mean?
examples.zh: 不好意思，refund 是什么意思？

examples.en: Did you say platform fifteen or fifty?
examples.zh: 你说的是 15 号站台还是 50 号站台？

examples.en: Sorry, I don't understand. Can you say that in a different way?
examples.zh: 抱歉，我没懂。你能换个说法吗？

mastery: 能在对话录音中识别出说话人在请求澄清
能针对没听懂的具体词或数字用合适的固定说法提问
在真实或模拟的服务对话中遇到不懂的关键信息时主动澄清并确认
commonErrors: 只会说 *What?，听起来不礼貌
问词义时说 *What is mean ...?，应为 What does ... mean?
boundaries: A1 的笼统请求重复（Can you repeat that?）见 kt:en-str-repair-basic；本知识点针对具体词句。
确认理解与请对方展开见 B1 的 kt:en-fn-check-understanding、kt:en-str-ask-elaborate。

primitives.binding: 困难时刻是对方用了生词或含糊指代，检查学习者用固定说法澄清而不是沉默或猜
请澄清固定说法 Sorry, what does X mean? / Do you mean…? 回合
*What? 与礼貌说法对比

kcs.label: 用近似词加手势表达
kcs.description: 不知道或想不起某个词时，用一个意思相近、更简单或更上位的词代替，并配合手势、指物或描述来补足意思，让交流继续下去。
forms: general word: a thing / a machine / a kind of fruit
It's like a ... / It's a kind of ...
You use it for + -ing
the thing for ...
point and say: this one / that thing
gesture with simple words: big, round, you know, like this

examples.en: I need the... the thing for opening wine. Like this.
examples.zh: 我需要那个……开红酒的东西，像这样。（配合手势）

examples.en: It's a kind of bird, but it can't fly. It lives in cold places.
examples.zh: 是一种鸟，但不会飞，生活在寒冷的地方。

mastery: 能根据别人的近似描述猜出所指的词
能为一组生词图片各说出一个近似说法（上位词或用途）
在信息差任务中遇到词汇空缺时，能用近似词加手势让对方理解，而不是放弃或改说中文
commonErrors: 卡住后直接说中文词或长时间沉默
近似词过于宽泛又不补充信息，只说 *a thing 而不说明用途或样子
boundaries: A1 的单纯手势和简单词求助见 kt:en-str-gesture-contact。
B2 的 kt:en-str-circumlocution 要求用较完整的改述准确表达，而不依赖手势。

primitives.binding: 卡词时用 a kind of…/a thing for…+手势继续，检查不换中文
先自己描述目标词再揭示对照

kcs.label: 句子重音与信息重点
kcs.description: 英语句子中实词（名词、主要动词、形容词、副词、否定词）通常重读，功能词通常不重读，形成轻重交替的节奏；说话人还会通过特别重读某个词来突出新信息或对比。
forms: content words stressed: I WANT to BUY a NEW BIKE.
function words unstressed: a, the, to, of, and, can, was
negatives stressed: I CAN'T come.
contrastive stress: I said TUESday, not THURSday.
new information gets main stress: — Where's your bag? — It's in the CAR.
stress-timed rhythm: stressed syllables at roughly regular intervals

examples.en: I'd like a BLACK coffee, not a WHITE one.
examples.zh: 我要黑咖啡，不是加奶的。（对比重读）

examples.en: She LIVES in LONdon but WORKS in OXford.
examples.zh: 她住在伦敦，但在牛津工作。

examples.en: I CAN swim. / I CAN'T swim.
examples.zh: 我会游泳。/ 我不会游泳。（can 肯定弱读、can't 重读）

mastery: 听一个句子能标出重读的词
能根据问题判断回答中哪个词应特别重读
朗读和对话中实词与功能词的轻重对比清楚，能用重音表达对比或纠正
commonErrors: 每个词都重读，节奏单调，听起来像在生气或强调
can 和 can't 都重读，导致听者难以区分肯定与否定
boundaries: 单词内部的重音见 kt:en-phon-word-stress；功能词弱读的具体形式见 kt:en-phon-weak-forms。
表达态度的语调模式见 B2 的 kt:en-phon-intonation。

primitives.binding: 标出信息重点重读词再跟读，比较重音分布（c56）
同句不同重音位置对应不同含义，听后选

kcs.label: 功能词的弱读
kcs.description: 在连续语流中，不重读的功能词（冠词、介词、助动词、代词等）常读成弱化形式，元音多变成 /ə/ 或脱落。掌握弱读既能让说话节奏自然，更能帮助听懂真实语速的英语。
forms: a /ə/, the /ðə/, and /ən/ or /n/, of /əv/ or /ə/
to /tə/, for /fə/, from /frəm/, at /ət/
can /kən/, was /wəz/, were /wə/, have /əv/, do /də/
her /ə/, them /ðəm/, you /jə/
strong form at the end of a sentence or when stressed: What are you looking AT /æt/?
common chunks: cup of tea /ˈkʌpəˈtiː/, fish and chips /ˌfɪʃnˈtʃɪps/

examples.en: I was at home. /aɪ wəz ət həʊm/
examples.zh: 我当时在家。（was 和 at 都弱读）

examples.en: Can you come for lunch? /kən jə kʌm fə lʌntʃ/
examples.zh: 你能来吃午饭吗？

examples.en: Yes, I can. /jes aɪ kæn/
examples.zh: 是的，我能。（句末用强读形式）

mastery: 听到含弱读的句子能写出被弱读的功能词（听写）
能判断某个功能词在句中应读强式还是弱式
朗读和日常说话时能自然使用常见弱读，语速和节奏接近自然
commonErrors: 把每个 to、of、and 都读得很重很清楚，节奏不自然
听写时漏掉弱读的功能词，如把 a cup of tea 写成 *a cup tea
句末该用强读时也弱读：*Yes, I /kən/.
boundaries: 词与词之间的连读与省音见 B1 的 kt:en-phon-linking。
弱读是自然语流中的常态，但慢速清晰朗读时使用强读也不算错误。

primitives.binding: 听写含 to/of/and/can 的句子，对齐看弱读处漏了什么（c47）
跟读时弱读功能词，比较节奏（c56）

kcs.label: 连贯叙述经历与事件
kcs.description: 把一段经历或一件事讲成有开头、经过、转折和结果的完整叙述：交代背景，按时间推进，说明事情如何出乎意料，以及最后的结果和感受。B1 要求叙述连贯，而不只是罗列句子。
forms: Background: It was ... / I was + -ing when ...
Sequence: First, ... Then ... After that, ... In the end, ...
Twist: Suddenly, ... / All of a sudden, ... / Unfortunately, ...
Earlier background: I had never ... before.
Result and reaction: In the end, ... / It turned out that ... / I felt so ...
Opening a story: Did I ever tell you about the time ...?

examples.en: We were driving home from the coast when the car suddenly stopped in the middle of nowhere.
examples.zh: 我们正从海边开车回家，车突然在一个荒凉的地方熄火了。

examples.en: I had never spoken to a famous person before, so I just stood there and smiled.
examples.zh: 我以前从没和名人说过话，所以只是站在那儿傻笑。

examples.en: In the end, a farmer towed us to the next village, and it turned out to be the best part of the trip.
examples.zh: 最后一位农民把我们拖到了下一个村子，结果那成了整趟旅行中最精彩的部分。

mastery: 听或读一段叙述时，能分出背景、主要事件、转折和结果。
能根据给定的时间线或图片，用恰当的过去时体和顺序词写出 6–8 句连贯叙述。
能即兴讲述一次真实经历约一分钟，交代背景和结果，并说明自己的感受。
commonErrors: 所有动词都用一般过去时，背景与主线不分：*I walked in the park, it rained. 应为 I was walking in the park and it was raining.
受汉语影响漏掉时态标记，直接用原形叙述：*Yesterday I go to the station and see him.
只罗列事件，缺少转折和结果，听者不知道故事的重点。
boundaries: 本知识点是功能层面的叙述组织；具体时体形式见 kt:en-past-continuous、kt:en-past-perfect，B2 的全面时体协调见 kt:en-narrative-tenses。
只谈“有没有做过”而不讲具体经过属于 kt:en-fn-past-experience。

primitives.binding: 过去进行（背景）vs 一般过去（主线）（c14）；检查 I was walking when it rained
按图讲一件事，区分背景句与事件句

kcs.label: 描述感受、情绪与态度
kcs.description: 描述自己或他人的感受、情绪和态度，并说明原因或程度。用于讲经历时的情感反应、回应别人的消息以及表达对事物的态度。
forms: I feel / felt + adjective (nervous, relieved, disappointed, embarrassed)
I was + -ed adjective + about / at / by / with ...
It was really + -ing adjective (frustrating, annoying, exciting)
It makes me feel ... / It drives me crazy when ...
I can't stand ... / I'm (not) keen on ... / I'm fed up with ...
Degree: a bit / quite / really / absolutely + adjective

examples.en: I was so relieved when the doctor said it was nothing serious.
examples.zh: 医生说没什么大问题时，我真是松了一口气。

examples.en: Waiting for exam results always makes me feel a bit anxious.
examples.zh: 等考试成绩总让我有点焦虑。

examples.en: She's fed up with people asking her when she's going to get married.
examples.zh: 她受够了别人总问她什么时候结婚。

mastery: 能区分一组情绪形容词的含义和强弱，如 annoyed / furious、pleased / delighted。
能在句子里选对 -ed / -ing 形容词和后接介词。
能讲述一件事并说明当时的感受和原因，或对别人的消息作出得体的情绪回应。
commonErrors: 混用 -ed / -ing：*I was very boring in the meeting. 应为 I was very bored.
介词搭配错误：*I'm worried for the exam. 应为 worried about；*angry to him 应为 angry with him。
照搬汉语“我很开心”只用 happy / sad 两三个词，无法表达程度和细微差别。
boundaries: -ed / -ing 形容词的形式规则见 kt:en-ed-ing-adjectives；本知识点关注在交际中描述情绪与态度。
对他人观点表示同意与否属于 kt:en-fn-opinion。

primitives.binding: bored/boring 等感受者 vs 引起者；材料是讲述经历中的感受
情绪形容词搭配 angry with/about 用例裁判

kcs.label: 过去完成时：更早的过去
kcs.description: had + 过去分词，表示在过去某个参照时间或事件之前已经发生或完成的事，即“过去的过去”。常用于叙述中补充背景或解释原因。
forms: subject + had + past participle
negative: hadn't + past participle
question: Had + subject + past participle ...?
with time markers: by the time, already, just, never ... before, when, after, because
contraction: I'd / she'd (= had)

examples.en: By the time we got to the cinema, the film had already started.
examples.zh: 我们到电影院的时候，电影已经开始了。

examples.en: She was nervous because she had never flown before.
examples.zh: 她很紧张，因为她以前从没坐过飞机。

examples.en: I didn't recognise him at first; he had grown a beard.
examples.zh: 我一开始没认出他，他留了胡子。

mastery: 能在时间线上标出两个过去事件的先后，并判断哪一个需要用过去完成时。
能正确构成 had + 过去分词的肯定、否定和疑问形式。
叙述时能在需要时用过去完成时补充更早的背景，而不是机械地给所有较早事件都用。
commonErrors: 当作“很久以前”的标记，在没有过去参照点时也用：*I had visited Paris in 2015. 应为 I visited Paris in 2015.
该用时漏用，导致先后不清：*When I arrived, she left.（意为她先走了）应为 she had left。
把 I'd 误解为 I would；或误用一般过去式而非过去分词：*had went。
boundaries: 用 before / after 已清楚表明顺序时，一般过去时通常也可以，过去完成时不是必须。
过去完成进行时（had been doing）见 kt:en-past-perfect-continuous；在第三条件句中的用法见 kt:en-third-conditional。

primitives.binding: 两个过去事件上轴，更早者用 had done；检查无参照点不用
had done vs did 按是否需回溯选（c35）

kcs.label: 现在完成与一般过去的选择
kcs.description: 在现在完成时与一般过去时之间作选择：事件与现在相关、时间未指明或时间段未结束时用现在完成时；有明确的已结束过去时间或在讲述具体经过时用一般过去时。
forms: present perfect: have/has + past participle; with ever, never, already, yet, just, so far, this week
past simple: with yesterday, last year, in 2019, ago, when I was ...
pattern: Have you ever ...? -> Yes, I have. I went there last summer.
unfinished period: I've drunk three coffees today. vs finished: I drank three coffees yesterday.
When ...? questions take past simple: When did you arrive?

examples.en: I've lost my phone, so I can't call you back.
examples.zh: 我把手机丢了，所以没法给你回电话。

examples.en: Have you ever tried Korean food? — Yes, I had it for the first time last month.
examples.zh: 你吃过韩国菜吗？——吃过，上个月第一次吃。

examples.en: He has worked here since 2020, but he worked in Shanghai before that.
examples.zh: 他从 2020 年起一直在这里工作，在那之前他在上海工作。

mastery: 能根据时间状语和语境判断应使用哪种时态并说明理由。
能在“经历提问 + 具体细节”的对话中从现在完成时自然转到一般过去时。
在口头或书面交流中谈近况、经历和具体事件时，时态选择基本正确。
commonErrors: 与明确过去时间连用：*I have seen him yesterday. 应为 I saw him yesterday.
汉语“了”“过”无对应时态区分，导致 *Did you ever go to Japan? 与 Have you ever been to Japan? 混用不分。
用 When 提问配现在完成时：*When have you arrived?
boundaries: 美式英语在 just / already / yet 句中常用一般过去时（Did you eat yet?），属于变体差异而非错误；见 kt:en-soc-varieties。
单个时态的形式与基本用法见 kt:en-present-perfect、kt:en-past-simple；持续时长见 kt:en-for-since、kt:en-present-perfect-continuous。

primitives.binding: 现在完成 vs 一般过去按是否有已结束时间选（c14）
事件是否与现在相连放上轴

kcs.label: 现在完成进行时：持续过程与时长
kcs.description: have/has been + -ing，表示从过去开始并持续到现在（或刚刚结束）的活动，强调过程和持续时长，也用来解释眼前可见的结果。
forms: subject + have/has been + verb-ing
How long have you been + -ing ...?
with for / since / all day / lately / recently
recent activity with visible result: You've been crying. / I've been running.
contrast: I've been reading this book (process) vs I've read this book (completed)

examples.en: I've been learning the guitar for about two years.
examples.zh: 我学吉他大约两年了。

examples.en: Your hands are covered in paint. What have you been doing?
examples.zh: 你满手都是颜料，你刚才在干什么？

examples.en: It's been raining since this morning, so the match might be cancelled.
examples.zh: 从早上起一直在下雨，比赛可能会取消。

mastery: 能识别句子强调的是过程/时长还是完成结果，并选择进行或非进行形式。
能用 How long have you been ...? 提问并用 for / since 回答。
能在谈近况或解释眼前状况时自然使用现在完成进行时。
commonErrors: 用一般现在时或现在进行时表示持续至今：*I am learning English for three years. / *I learn here since 2021.
与状态动词连用：*I've been knowing her for years. 应为 I've known her for years.
强调完成数量时仍用进行形式：*I've been writing three emails. 应为 I've written three emails.
boundaries: 完成结果、次数和数量用 kt:en-present-perfect；for / since 的选择见 kt:en-for-since。
live、work 等动词两种形式意义差别很小（I've lived / I've been living here for years）。

primitives.binding: 从过去延续到现在的过程上轴，选 have been doing；检查 *I am learning…for three years
have done（结果/次数）vs have been doing（过程/时长）

kcs.label: for / since 表达时长与起点
kcs.description: for 后接一段时长（three days, ages），since 后接起始时间点或事件（2019, Monday, I was a child），主要与完成时连用表示持续到现在的时间。
forms: for + period: for ten minutes, for two years, for ages, for a long time
since + point: since 8 o'clock, since Monday, since 2018, since last summer
since + clause: since I moved here, since we left school
How long ...? -> for / since answers
It's (been) + period + since + past simple: It's been two years since we met.

examples.en: We've known each other since primary school.
examples.zh: 我们从小学起就认识了。

examples.en: She has been waiting for over an hour.
examples.zh: 她已经等了一个多小时了。

examples.en: It's been ages since I last went swimming.
examples.zh: 我已经好久没去游泳了。

mastery: 能对一组时间表达正确归类为 for 或 since。
能把 I started ... in ... 改写成 I've ... since ... / for ...。
能用 for / since 回答 How long ...? 并谈论自己的经历与习惯。
commonErrors: since 后接时长：*since three years. 应为 for three years.
受汉语“……了三年”影响用一般现在时：*I live here for three years.
since 从句误用完成时：*since I have moved here. 通常为 since I moved here。
boundaries: for 也可用于一般过去时表示已结束的时长（I lived there for five years），since 一般不行。
since 表原因（= because）属于连接词用法，不在此知识点内；时态选择见 kt:en-present-perfect-continuous。

primitives.binding: for+时长 vs since+起点；检查 *since three years
在轴上标起点还是标区间

kcs.label: would 表达过去反复行为
kcs.description: 用 would + 动词原形描述过去反复发生的动作或习惯，多用于怀旧叙述。与 used to 不同，would 不能表示过去的状态。
forms: subject + would ('d) + base verb (repeated past action)
often follows a used to sentence that sets the scene
with frequency words: always, often, sometimes, every summer
not with state verbs: *would live / *would have / *would be (state)

examples.en: When I was little, my grandmother would tell me stories every night.
examples.zh: 我小时候，奶奶每天晚上都会给我讲故事。

examples.en: We used to live near a river, and in summer we'd swim there after school.
examples.zh: 我们以前住在河边，夏天放学后会去那里游泳。

mastery: 能判断句中 would 表示过去习惯还是条件或礼貌请求。
能判断哪些句子可用 would 替换 used to（动作可以，状态不行）。
讲述童年或往事时能交替使用 used to 和 would 描述习惯。
commonErrors: 用于状态：*I would have long hair when I was a teenager. 应为 I used to have long hair.
叙述一开始就用 would 而没有过去时间框架，听者会误以为是假设。
boundaries: used to 的形式与状态用法见 kt:en-used-to；would 的条件用法见 kt:en-second-conditional。
只发生一次的过去事件用一般过去时，不用 would 或 used to。

primitives.binding: would（反复动作）vs used to（动作与状态）；检查状态不用 would
过去反复动作在轴上的分布

kcs.label: 表达观点、同意与不同意
kcs.description: 陈述自己的观点，询问他人的看法，并表示同意、部分同意或不同意，同时给出理由。不同意时要用缓和表达保持礼貌。
forms: I think / I don't think (that) ... / In my opinion, ... / Personally, I feel ...
What do you think about ...? / How do you feel about ...?
I agree (with you). / I totally agree. / That's true.
I'm not sure about that. / I see your point, but ... / I don't really agree, because ...
So do I. / Neither do I. / Me too.

examples.en: In my opinion, public transport should be free for students.
examples.zh: 我认为学生乘公共交通应该免费。

examples.en: I see your point, but I don't think working from home suits everyone.
examples.zh: 我明白你的意思，但我不认为在家办公适合每一个人。

examples.en: I totally agree with you about the new park; it's made a big difference.
examples.zh: 关于新公园我完全同意你，它带来了很大变化。

mastery: 听一段讨论能判断说话人是同意、部分同意还是不同意。
能用至少三种不同表达提出观点并附上理由。
在讨论中能礼貌地表示不同意，并用 because 等给出理由。
commonErrors: 受汉语“我同意”影响加 be：*I am agree with you. 应为 I agree with you.
否定位置不自然：*I think it isn't a good idea. 英语更常说 I don't think it's a good idea.
直接说 You're wrong. 显得生硬，缺少缓和语。
boundaries: 系统论证与说服属于 kt:en-fn-argument、kt:en-fn-persuade（B2）。
对照两种观点的 on the one hand 结构见 kt:en-contrasting-opinions。

primitives.binding: 表达观点—同意—部分同意—反对回合；检查 I agree 无 be
I totally disagree vs I'm not sure I agree 强度（c17）

kcs.label: because / so 的因果与结果
kcs.description: because 引出原因，so 引出结果，把两个分句连成因果关系。B1 要求在说理时稳定使用两者并区分方向。
forms: result + because + reason: I stayed home because I was ill.
reason + , so + result: I was ill, so I stayed home.
Because + reason, + result (sentence-initial in writing)
because of + noun: because of the rain
Why ...? -> Because ... (spoken short answer)

examples.en: The shop was closed, so we bought bread at the petrol station.
examples.zh: 商店关门了，所以我们在加油站买了面包。

examples.en: I prefer the bus because I can read on the way.
examples.zh: 我更喜欢坐公交，因为路上可以看书。

examples.en: The flight was delayed because of the snow.
examples.zh: 航班因为下雪延误了。

mastery: 能判断句子中哪一部分是原因、哪一部分是结果。
能把 because 句与 so 句互相转换，意义不变。
表达观点或叙述时能自然用 because / so 给出理由和结果。
commonErrors: 受汉语“因为……所以……”影响同时使用：*Because it rained, so we stayed home.
because 后接名词短语：*because the rain 应为 because of the rain。
书面中单独把 Because 从句当完整句：*Because I was tired.
boundaries: 较正式的因果连接（therefore, as a result, due to）见 kt:en-cause-effect-linkers。
so 作程度副词（so tired）属于 kt:en-too-enough。

primitives.binding: 因果两句用 because 或 so 接，只用一个（c16）；检查不叠用
because/so 处押后句是原因还是结果（c59）

kcs.label: 因果与推论连接（as a result / therefore / due to）
kcs.description: 用 as a result、therefore、that's why、due to、since、as 等表达原因、结果和推论，常见于书面说明和较正式的讲述，比 because / so 更能连接句子和段落。
forms: Sentence linkers: As a result, ... / Therefore, ... / For this reason, ... / That's why ...
Reason clauses: as + clause, since + clause
Prepositional: due to / owing to / because of + noun phrase
Result: ..., which means (that) ...
Punctuation: ... . Therefore, ... / ...; as a result, ...

examples.en: The road was flooded. As a result, the school closed early.
examples.zh: 道路被淹了，因此学校提前放学。

examples.en: Since you've already seen the film, why don't you choose something else?
examples.zh: 既然你已经看过这部电影，为什么不选别的呢？

examples.en: The concert was cancelled due to the singer's illness.
examples.zh: 因为歌手生病，音乐会取消了。

mastery: 能区分连接词后接的是分句还是名词短语（as a result + 句子，due to + 名词）。
能用合适的连接词和标点把两个独立句连成因果关系。
在短文或帖子中能变换使用多种因果连接，而不只重复 because / so。
commonErrors: due to 后接分句：*due to it was raining 应为 due to the rain / because it was raining。
把 therefore 当连词用逗号连两句：*It was late, therefore we left. 书面应用句号或分号。
语域不当：口语聊天中频繁用 therefore 显得生硬。
boundaries: 基础的 because / so 见 kt:en-because-so；转折对照见 kt:en-however、kt:en-contrast-linkers。
since 表时间起点见 kt:en-for-since。

primitives.binding: due to+名词 vs because+从句 vs as a result 句间；检查 *due to it was
遇 therefore/as a result 押后句方向（c33）

kcs.label: however 的句间转折
kcs.description: however 连接两个句子，表示后句与前句形成转折或意外，常放在句首并接逗号。功能上相当于句间的 but，但更书面。
forms: Sentence 1. However, sentence 2.
Sentence 1; however, sentence 2.
mid-position: The hotel, however, was very noisy.
spoken alternatives: but, though (end position)

examples.en: The flat is small. However, it's very close to the station.
examples.zh: 这套公寓很小，不过离车站很近。

examples.en: Most people enjoyed the tour; however, a few found it too long.
examples.zh: 大多数人喜欢这次游览，不过也有几个人觉得太长了。

mastery: 能识别 however 前后两句的转折关系。
能把 but 连接的复合句改写成用 However 开头的两句话，标点正确。
在短文或邮件中能用 however 引出相反信息。
commonErrors: 当作连词用逗号连接两句：*It was cheap, however it was very good quality.
与 but 同用：*But however, ...
受汉语“虽然……但是……”影响写成 *Although it was cheap, however it was good.
boundaries: however + 形容词（however hard you try）表示“无论多么”，不属于本知识点。
对照两事物的 whereas / while 见 kt:en-contrast-linkers；although / despite 见 B2 的 kt:en-although、kt:en-despite。

primitives.binding: however 连两句需句号或分号，与 but 对照；检查逗号接句
遇 However 押转折（c33）

kcs.label: whereas / while / on the other hand 的对照
kcs.description: 用 whereas、while、on the other hand 对照两个人、事物或情况的不同之处，强调并列的差异，而不是意外或让步。
forms: clause + whereas / while + clause: My brother loves sport, whereas I prefer reading.
While + clause, clause.
Sentence. On the other hand, sentence.
in contrast / by contrast (written)
unlike + noun: Unlike my sister, I ...

examples.en: Trains are faster, whereas buses are much cheaper.
examples.zh: 火车更快，而公交车便宜得多。

examples.en: While the north of the country is dry, the south gets a lot of rain.
examples.zh: 这个国家北部干燥，而南部雨水很多。

examples.en: Living in the city is exciting. On the other hand, it can be very expensive.
examples.zh: 住在城里很刺激，但另一方面也可能很贵。

mastery: 能区分 whereas（对照）与 however / although（转折或让步）的意义差别。
能用 whereas / while / unlike 写出比较两样事物的句子。
比较两种选择时能组织出对照清楚的一段话。
commonErrors: 单独用 On the other hand 而前文没有对照对象，语义悬空。
while 的“同时”与“而”两种意义混淆，导致误读。
whereas 之后另起一句：*Cats are quiet. Whereas dogs are noisy.
boundaries: 对照两种观点的 on the one hand ... on the other hand 见 kt:en-contrasting-opinions。
句间转折 however 见 kt:en-however；让步 although 见 kt:en-although。

primitives.binding: 两事物对照用 whereas/while 接成一句（c16）；检查有对照对象
标出对照的两边

kcs.label: on the one hand… on the other hand
kcs.description: 用 on the one hand ... on the other hand 等固定框架把同一问题的两方面观点或利弊并列呈现，再给出自己的结论。常用于讨论和短文。
forms: On the one hand, ... On the other hand, ...
Some people think ..., while others believe ...
There are advantages and disadvantages to ...
One advantage is ... / The main disadvantage is ...
All in all, ... / Overall, I think ...

examples.en: On the one hand, online shopping saves time. On the other hand, you can't try things on.
examples.zh: 一方面，网购省时间；另一方面，你没法试穿。

examples.en: Some people think homework is essential, while others believe it causes too much stress.
examples.zh: 有些人认为作业必不可少，另一些人则认为它带来太大压力。

mastery: 读或听一段讨论时能找出正反两方面的观点。
能用 on the one hand / on the other hand 框架列出某话题的利弊。
能写一段平衡的观点短文，最后给出自己的立场。
commonErrors: 只用 On the other hand 却缺第一面，或两面意思并不对立。
介词错误：*In the one hand / *At the other hand。
列完两面后没有结论，论述显得不完整。
boundaries: 对照两个事物的事实差异见 kt:en-contrast-linkers；表达自己的观点见 kt:en-fn-opinion。
B2 的完整论证结构见 kt:en-fn-argument、kt:en-skill-write-essay。

primitives.binding: on the one hand/on the other hand 两面结构，检查两面都在且对立（c32）
从一面观点扩成两面段落

kcs.label: 开启与结束交谈
kcs.description: 在非正式或半正式场合主动开启交谈（打招呼、找话题、搭话），以及得体地结束交谈（表示要走、总结、道别），不显得突兀。
forms: Opening: Excuse me, is anyone sitting here? / Hi, I don't think we've met. / How's it going?
Small talk starters: Lovely weather, isn't it? / Have you been here before?
Signalling the end: Anyway, I'd better get going. / Well, it was nice talking to you.
Closing: See you later. / Let's keep in touch. / Take care.

examples.en: Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm Lin, I work with Sarah.
examples.zh: 你好，我们好像没见过。我是林，和 Sarah 一起工作。

examples.en: Anyway, I'd better go — my bus is coming. It was nice chatting with you!
examples.zh: 好啦，我得走了，我的车来了。和你聊天很开心！

mastery: 能识别对话中预示要结束谈话的信号（Anyway, ... / Well, ...）。
能用合适的开场和结束语完成一段对话框架。
在角色扮演中能主动与陌生人搭话，并在 2–3 轮后自然结束。
commonErrors: 直接说 *I go now. / Bye. 结束谈话，缺少过渡，显得生硬。
直译汉语寒暄：*Have you eaten? 在英语中通常不是问候。
boundaries: 基本问候与告别见 kt:en-fn-greetings；谈话中途的打断与转题见 kt:en-fn-manage-turns。
正式会议的开场属于 B2 的 kt:en-fn-initiative。

primitives.binding: 开启与收尾回合：Anyway, I'd better go…；检查不突然 Bye
对朋友 vs 对同事的收尾措辞

kcs.label: 确认与澄清理解
kcs.description: 在交谈中确认自己是否理解对方、对方是否理解自己，通过复述、追问或检查来避免误解。
forms: Checking you understood: So you mean ...? / Do you mean ...? / Are you saying that ...?
Checking the listener: Do you know what I mean? / Does that make sense? / Is that clear?
Confirming details: Sorry, was that Tuesday or Thursday?
Paraphrase check: So, in other words, ...

examples.en: So you mean we should meet at the station, not at the cinema?
examples.zh: 你的意思是我们在车站见，而不是电影院？

examples.en: You press this button first, then the green one. Does that make sense?
examples.zh: 先按这个键，再按绿色那个。明白了吗？

mastery: 能区分“确认自己理解”和“检查对方理解”两类表达。
能用 So you mean ...? 复述对方的话加以确认。
在获取或给出信息的对话中，能在关键细节处主动确认，避免误解。
commonErrors: 直译“你懂吗”：*Do you understand me? 语气可能显得居高临下，Does that make sense? 更得体。
只说 Yes 或点头假装理解，不主动确认。
boundaries: 请对方重复或放慢见 kt:en-str-ask-clarification；请对方展开解释见 kt:en-str-ask-elaborate。
本知识点强调确认已有信息，不包括发现自己出错后的修正（kt:en-str-self-correct）。

primitives.binding: Does that make sense? / So you mean…? 确认回合
*Do you understand me? 居高临下 vs 得体说法

kcs.label: 打断、换题与恢复话题
kcs.description: 在谈话中礼貌地插话、转换话题，以及在被打断后回到原话题，使交流顺畅推进。
forms: Interrupting: Sorry to interrupt, but ... / Can I just say something?
Changing topic: By the way, ... / Talking of ..., ... / That reminds me, ...
Resuming: Anyway, as I was saying, ... / Going back to what I said ...
Holding the turn: Just a moment, let me finish.

examples.en: Sorry to interrupt, but the taxi is already outside.
examples.zh: 抱歉打断一下，出租车已经在外面了。

examples.en: By the way, did you hear that Tom got the job?
examples.zh: 对了，你听说 Tom 得到那份工作了吗？

examples.en: Anyway, as I was saying, the hotel was lovely.
examples.zh: 总之，我刚才说到，那家酒店很不错。

mastery: 能识别对话中插话、转题和回到原话题的表达。
能在给定情境中选用合适的插话或转题表达。
在小组讨论中能礼貌插话，并在被打断后自然回到原话题。
commonErrors: 直接插话不加缓冲：*Wait, I want to say ...，显得不礼貌。
滥用 By the way 引出与上文直接相关的内容。
boundaries: 开启与结束整段交谈见 kt:en-fn-open-close；邀请他人参与讨论见 B2 的 kt:en-fn-invite-participation。
well / anyway 作为一般口语组织标记见 kt:en-informal-spoken-markers。

primitives.binding: 困难时刻是对方跑题或打断，检查学习者打断、换题、拉回话题的说法
打断—换题—回到话题回合：Sorry to interrupt…/Going back to…（c45）
*Wait, I want to say 生硬 vs 缓冲说法

kcs.label: 口语中的组织标记（well / anyway / so）
kcs.term: Markers to structure informal spoken discourse
kcs.description: well、anyway、so、right、I mean、you know 等口语标记，用来开始话轮、转换方向、拖延思考或修正说法，帮助组织非正式口语，但本身不承载命题内容。
forms: Well, ... (hesitating, softening a reply)
So, ... (starting, summing up)
Anyway, ... (returning or closing)
Right / OK, ... (moving to the next step)
I mean, ... (clarifying, correcting)
You know, ... / Actually, ...

examples.en: Well, I'm not sure it's a good idea, to be honest.
examples.zh: 嗯，说实话，我不确定这是个好主意。

examples.en: Right, let's start with the first question.
examples.zh: 好，我们从第一个问题开始。

examples.en: It was cheap — I mean, not cheap, but cheaper than I expected.
examples.zh: 挺便宜的——我是说，不算便宜，但比我预想的便宜。

mastery: 听对话时能判断 well / anyway / I mean 等标记的作用（犹豫、转回、修正）。
能在对话填空中选择恰当的标记。
自己说话时能用若干标记组织话轮，不过度重复同一个。
commonErrors: 过度使用 you know / like，影响清晰度。
在正式书面语中使用 well / anyway 开头。
把汉语“那个……”“就是……”直译为 *that ... / *is ...。
boundaries: 正式场合的路标语（firstly, to sum up）见 kt:en-formal-signposting。
具体插话与转题功能见 kt:en-fn-manage-turns；为争取时间的策略见 kt:en-str-gain-time。

primitives.binding: 检查 well / anyway / so 在接话、拖延、转回话题时的位置
在口语转写中标出 well/anyway/so 的组织功能（c45）
you know/like 过度使用裁判

kcs.label: 附加问句
kcs.description: 陈述句后加简短反问（isn't it? / didn't you? / can't she?），用于确认信息或寻求认同。肯定句接否定附加问，否定句接肯定附加问；助动词与时态须与主句一致。语调决定是真问还是求认同。
forms: positive statement + negative tag: You're tired, aren't you?
negative statement + positive tag: She doesn't eat meat, does she?
auxiliary/modal matches main clause: has / did / can / will / would
special cases: I'm late, aren't I? / Let's go, shall we? / Open the door, will you?
falling intonation = expecting agreement; rising = real question

examples.en: You've been to this restaurant before, haven't you?
examples.zh: 你以前来过这家餐厅，对吧？

examples.en: He won't mind if we're a bit late, will he?
examples.zh: 我们晚到一点他不会介意吧？

examples.en: It wasn't a very good match, was it?
examples.zh: 那场比赛不怎么样，是吧？

mastery: 能为各种时态和情态动词的陈述句选择正确的附加问句。
能听辨附加问句的升调与降调，判断说话人是在提问还是求认同。
在闲聊中能用附加问句寻求认同或确认信息。
commonErrors: 受汉语“……，对吗？”影响一律用 *is it? / *isn't it? / *right?：*You like coffee, isn't it?
助动词或时态不一致：*She went home, doesn't she?
回答否定附加问时按汉语逻辑：She isn't coming, is she? — *Yes（意为“对，她不来”）应为 No, she isn't.
boundaries: 简短回应与回声问（So did I / Did you?）见 kt:en-short-responses。
附加问句的语调与 kt:en-phon-intonation-questions 相关；本知识点以形式和功能为主。

primitives.binding: 助动词+人称代词、肯否反转推到新句；检查不一律 isn't it/right
附加问句升调（求证）vs 降调（求同）

kcs.label: 简短回应（So did I / Did you? / Neither do I）
kcs.description: 用助动词构成的简短回应来参与对话：表示自己也一样（So did I / Neither do I），表示感兴趣或惊讶的回声问（Did you? / Have you?），以及简短答语（Yes, I did）。
forms: So + auxiliary + subject: So did I. / So am I. / So have I.
Neither / Nor + auxiliary + subject: Neither do I. / Nor can I.
Reply questions: Did you? / Was it? / Haven't you?
Contrast: I didn't. / I did.
informal: Me too. / Me neither.

examples.en: I went to bed really late last night. — So did I.
examples.zh: 我昨晚睡得很晚。——我也是。

examples.en: I haven't finished the report yet. — Neither have I.
examples.zh: 我报告还没写完。——我也没有。

examples.en: We saw a whale on the boat trip. — Did you? That's amazing!
examples.zh: 我们坐船时看到了一头鲸。——真的吗？太棒了！

mastery: 能根据前句的时态和肯否选择正确的助动词和 So / Neither。
能用回声问表示惊讶或兴趣。
在对话中能自然用简短回应表示认同、对比或兴趣，让对话继续。
commonErrors: 助动词不匹配：I went there. — *So do I. 应为 So did I.
否定句后用 too 或 So：*I don't like it. — Me too. / *So don't I. 应为 Me neither / Neither do I.
Neither 句再加否定：*Neither don't I.
boundaries: 陈述句后的附加问句见 kt:en-question-tags。
正式场合的反应与评论见 kt:en-fn-reactions（B2）。

kcs.label: 请对方澄清或展开
kcs.term: Asking someone to clarify or elaborate
kcs.description: 当对方说得太笼统或你只听懂一部分时，请对方举例、解释含义或说得更具体，以获得更完整的信息并显示你在认真听。
forms: What do you mean by ...?
Could you give me an example?
Could you explain that a bit more?
In what way? / Why do you say that?
Can you be more specific?

examples.en: You said the job was 'challenging'. What do you mean by that?
examples.zh: 你说这份工作“有挑战性”，具体指什么？

examples.en: That's interesting. Could you give me an example?
examples.zh: 很有意思。能举个例子吗？

mastery: 能区分“请重复”和“请解释/展开”的不同请求。
能在听到模糊说法时选用恰当表达追问。
在讨论或采访中能主动追问细节，使对方给出例子或理由。
commonErrors: 只会说 *Pardon? / What? 请对方重复，而实际需要的是解释。
直译“什么意思”：*What's your meaning? 应为 What do you mean?
boundaries: 请对方重复或放慢见 kt:en-str-ask-clarification；确认自己理解见 kt:en-fn-check-understanding。
B2 的追问以推进讨论见 kt:en-str-follow-up。

primitives.binding: 请对方展开 Could you give an example? / What do you mean by…? 回合

kcs.label: 意识到误解或错误时自我修正
kcs.description: 说话时发现自己用错词、说错事实或造成误解，及时停下并纠正，使交流不偏离。
forms: Sorry, I mean ...
No, wait — it was ..., not ...
What I meant was ...
Let me put that another way.
Sorry, I said ..., but I meant ...

examples.en: The meeting is on Tuesday — sorry, I mean Thursday.
examples.zh: 会议在星期二——抱歉，我是说星期四。

examples.en: I didn't mean the old library; what I meant was the new one near the park.
examples.zh: 我不是说旧图书馆，我指的是公园旁边那个新的。

mastery: 听自己的录音或他人的话时能发现造成误解的错误。
能用 Sorry, I mean ... 等表达纠正口误。
在对话中当对方的反应显示误解时，能主动澄清并改正。
commonErrors: 发现错误后默默跳过，导致对方继续误解。
纠正过多细小语法错误，反而打断表达流畅。
boundaries: 本知识点针对已经造成或可能造成误解的错误，不要求纠正每个小错。
用其他说法绕过不会的词见 kt:en-str-approximate、kt:en-str-circumlocution。

primitives.binding: 录对话自转写，标出该自我修正处并重说（c55）

kcs.label: will 与 going to 的预测比较
kcs.term: Will and going to for prediction
kcs.description: will 与 going to 都能做预测：will 多基于个人看法、经验或推测；going to 多基于眼前证据，表示某事“看样子要发生”。
forms: will + base verb: I think it'll be a great party.
be going to + base verb (present evidence): Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.
with I think / I'm sure / probably / I bet + will
won't for negative predictions
Be careful! You're going to fall.

examples.en: Look at the traffic. We're going to miss the start of the film.
examples.zh: 看这交通，我们要错过电影开头了。

examples.en: Don't worry, I'm sure you'll pass the interview.
examples.zh: 别担心，我相信你能通过面试。

examples.en: In twenty years, most cars will probably be electric.
examples.zh: 二十年后大多数汽车可能会是电动的。

mastery: 能根据语境中是否有眼前证据判断 will 或 going to 更自然。
能看图用 going to 说出即将发生的事。
能用 will 及程度词对未来趋势作出个人预测。
commonErrors: 漏掉 be：*It going to rain.
will 后加 to 或变形：*It will to rain / *will rains。
两者区别在很多语境里并不绝对，学习者常过度规则化，认为某一种“错了”。
boundaries: 表示计划与决定的 will / going to 见 kt:en-will-future、kt:en-going-to。
确定度梯度见 kt:en-certainty-scale；将来进行时见 kt:en-future-continuous。

primitives.binding: 有现场迹象 going to vs 个人看法 will（c14）；检查 be 不漏

kcs.label: will / probably / may / might 的确定度梯度
kcs.description: 用 will、will probably、may、might、probably won't、won't 等表达对未来或现在情况的不同把握程度，从确定到不可能形成一条梯度。
forms: will definitely / certainly (≈100%)
will probably / is likely to
may / might / could (≈50% or less)
probably won't / is unlikely to
definitely won't (≈0%)
word order: will probably / probably won't

examples.en: I'll probably be home by seven, but I might be a bit late.
examples.zh: 我大概七点到家，但也可能会晚一点。

examples.en: It may snow tomorrow, so take a warm coat.
examples.zh: 明天可能下雪，带件厚外套吧。

examples.en: She probably won't come — she's got an exam on Monday.
examples.zh: 她多半不会来，她星期一有考试。

mastery: 能把一组表达按确定程度从高到低排序。
能把 probably 放在 will 之后、won't 之前的正确位置。
能对未来计划或事件用不同确定度表达自己的判断。
commonErrors: probably 位置错误：*I probably will come / *I won't probably come（前者口语中也见，但 I'll probably come 更常见；后者应为 I probably won't）。
might 后加 to：*It might to rain.
把 maybe 当情态动词用：*It maybe rain tomorrow.
boundaries: may / might 的基本形式见 kt:en-may-might；基于证据的 must / can't 推断见 kt:en-must-cant-deduction。
B2 的推测表达见 kt:en-modal-speculation、kt:en-fn-speculate。

primitives.binding: will/probably/may/might 确定度梯度排序（c34）；检查 probably 位置
probably 放 will 后、won't 前

kcs.label: 将来进行时
kcs.description: will be + -ing，表示将来某一时刻正在进行的动作，或按常规安排自然会发生的事；也可用于委婉询问别人的计划。
forms: subject + will be + verb-ing
with time points: at this time tomorrow, at 8 tonight, this time next week
polite enquiry: Will you be using the car this evening?
background for another event: I'll be working when you arrive.

examples.en: This time next week, I'll be lying on a beach in Thailand.
examples.zh: 下周这个时候我会正躺在泰国的沙滩上。

examples.en: Don't call at nine — we'll be having dinner.
examples.zh: 九点别打电话，那时我们正在吃晚饭。

examples.en: Will you be using the printer this afternoon?
examples.zh: 你今天下午要用打印机吗？

mastery: 能识别句中描述的是将来某时刻正在进行的动作。
能根据时间表说出某人在将来某时刻正在做什么。
能用 Will you be ...? 委婉询问他人安排。
commonErrors: 漏掉 be：*I will working at 8.
用一般将来时代替，失去“正在进行”之意：*At 8 tomorrow I will work.（语法可接受但意义不同）
与状态动词连用：*I'll be knowing the results.
boundaries: 将来某时之前已完成的事用 kt:en-future-perfect（B2）。
一般预测见 kt:en-future-prediction；已安排的计划见 kt:en-present-continuous-future。

kcs.label: must / can't 的推断
kcs.description: 根据证据对现在的情况作出有把握的推断：must 表示“一定是”，can't 表示“不可能是”。这里的 must 不表示义务。
forms: must + base verb / be: She must be tired.
can't + base verb / be: That can't be Tom.
must be + -ing: They must be sleeping.
negative of deduction is can't, not mustn't
contrast: might / could = less certain

examples.en: The lights are off. They must be out.
examples.zh: 灯都关了，他们一定出去了。

examples.en: That can't be her car — she sold it last year.
examples.zh: 那不可能是她的车，她去年就卖了。

examples.en: You've been travelling all day. You must be exhausted.
examples.zh: 你奔波了一整天，一定累坏了。

mastery: 能区分 must 表推断和表义务的用法。
能根据给定线索用 must / can't / might 作出推断。
能在讨论图片或情境时用推断表达说明理由。
commonErrors: 否定推断用 mustn't：*He mustn't be at home. 应为 He can't be at home.
受汉语“一定”影响用 must 表将来预测：*It must rain tomorrow. 应为 It's going to / will probably rain。
boundaries: 对过去的推断（must have / can't have）见 B2 的 kt:en-past-modal-deduction。
must 表义务见 kt:en-must-mustnt、kt:en-must-vs-have-to。

primitives.binding: must/might/can't 推断梯度两端；检查否定推断用 can't 而非 mustn't
He must be tired 判断是推断还是义务

kcs.label: must 与 have to 的区别
kcs.description: must 与 have to 都表示必须：must 常表示说话人自己认为必要或规定性的书面要求；have to 多表示外部规定或客观要求。否定时意义差别很大：mustn't 是禁止，don't have to 是不必。
forms: must + base verb (speaker's view, rules, notices)
have to / has to + base verb (external obligation)
mustn't = it is not allowed
don't have to = it is not necessary
past and future: had to / will have to (must has no past form)

examples.en: I must call my mum tonight — it's her birthday.
examples.zh: 我今晚一定得给妈妈打电话，今天是她生日。

examples.en: You don't have to wear a suit, but you mustn't wear jeans.
examples.zh: 你不必穿西装，但不能穿牛仔裤。

examples.en: We had to wait two hours at the border.
examples.zh: 我们在边境不得不等了两个小时。

mastery: 能区分 mustn't 与 don't have to 的意义。
能把 must 句改成过去或将来时（had to / will have to）。
能介绍学校、工作或某地的规则，正确区分义务、禁止和不必要。
commonErrors: 把 mustn't 当作“不必”：*You mustn't come tomorrow（本意是不必来）。
用 must 表达过去：*Yesterday I must work late. 应为 I had to work late.
have to 第三人称变化错误：*She have to go.
boundaries: 英式英语中两者的主观/客观区分较明显，美式英语更普遍用 have to；口语里 have got to 也常见。
need to / needn't 见 kt:en-need-to；must 表推断见 kt:en-must-cant-deduction。

primitives.binding: must（说话人要求）vs have to（外部规则），mustn't vs don't have to

kcs.label: ought to
kcs.description: ought to + 动词原形，表示建议或应做的事，意义接近 should，但略正式、使用频率较低；也可表示按常理应该发生的事。
forms: subject + ought to + base verb
negative: ought not to / oughtn't to (rare; shouldn't is more common)
expectation: The train ought to be here soon.
questions usually use should instead

examples.en: You ought to see a doctor about that cough.
examples.zh: 你那咳嗽应该去看看医生。

examples.en: We ought to leave now if we want to get a seat.
examples.zh: 想有座位的话，我们现在就该走了。

mastery: 能识别 ought to 与 should 的意义相同。
能把 should 句改写为 ought to 句，保留 to。
提建议时能在 should、ought to、had better 之间适当选择。
commonErrors: 漏掉 to：*You ought see a doctor.
按普通动词变形：*She oughts to / *doesn't ought to。
boundaries: 基本建议 should 见 kt:en-should-advice；对过去的评价 ought to have / should have 见 kt:en-past-modals-evaluation。
美式英语中 ought to 的否定和疑问形式很少见。

primitives.binding: ought to + 原形、否定 ought not to；检查 to 不漏

kcs.label: need to / needn't / don't need to
kcs.description: need to 表示必要，don't need to 与 needn't 表示没有必要。needn't 是情态动词形式，较英式、较正式；don't need to 在各变体中都常用。
forms: need to + base verb / needs to
don't / doesn't need to + base verb
needn't + base verb (modal, mainly British)
Do I need to ...? / Need I ...? (formal, rare)
past: didn't need to

examples.en: You don't need to bring anything — we've got plenty of food.
examples.zh: 你什么都不用带，我们吃的很多。

examples.en: She needs to renew her passport before the trip.
examples.zh: 她得在旅行前更新护照。

examples.en: You needn't wait for me; I'll take a taxi.
examples.zh: 你不必等我，我会打车。

mastery: 能区分 needn't / don't need to（不必）与 mustn't（禁止）。
能正确使用 need to 的第三人称和疑问形式。
能在安排事务时说明哪些事必须做、哪些不必做。
commonErrors: needn't 后加 to：*You needn't to come.
情态与实义用法混合：*He needs not go / *He doesn't need go。
boundaries: needn't have done（做了但其实不必）与 didn't need to 的区别见 B2 的 kt:en-neednt-have。
must / have to 的义务区分见 kt:en-must-vs-have-to。

kcs.label: should have / might have / could have
kcs.description: 情态动词 + have + 过去分词，回头评价或推想过去：should have 表示本应做而没做（遗憾或批评），could have 表示本来有可能，might have 表示可能已经发生或本来可能发生。
forms: should(n't) have + past participle (criticism, regret)
could have + past participle (possibility not taken)
might / may have + past participle (possible past event)
spoken weak forms: should've /ʃʊdəv/, could've, might've
ought to have + past participle

examples.en: I should have checked the weather before we left.
examples.zh: 我们出发前我真该查一下天气。

examples.en: You could have hurt yourself — be more careful next time.
examples.zh: 你差点伤到自己，下次小心点。

examples.en: He's not answering. He might have gone to bed early.
examples.zh: 他没接电话，可能早睡了。

mastery: 能判断句子表达的是遗憾/批评、未实现的可能还是对过去的推测。
能对给定的过去情境用 should have / could have 作出评价。
能在讲述失误或意外时表达遗憾并推想其他可能。
commonErrors: 按读音写成 *should of / *could of。
用过去式代替过去分词：*should have went。
受汉语“本来应该”影响只用 should + 原形：*Yesterday I should go to the doctor.
boundaries: 以证据推断过去的 must have / can't have 见 B2 的 kt:en-past-modal-deduction。
更全面的过去情态见 kt:en-modals-past（C1）；表达后悔的 wish 见 kt:en-wish-regret。

primitives.binding: should have/could have/might have 按评价/机会/可能选；检查 *should of
should've 弱读与 should of 拼写对照

kcs.label: 第二条件句：与现实有距离的假设
kcs.description: If + 一般过去时, would + 动词原形，谈论现在或将来不真实、不太可能或纯属想象的情况及其结果。这里的过去式表示与现实的“距离”，而不是过去时间。
forms: If + past simple, would / could / might + base verb
would + base verb + if + past simple
If I were you, I'd ... (advice)
If + subject + were (formal) / was (informal)
What would you do if ...?

examples.en: If I had more free time, I'd learn to play the piano.
examples.zh: 要是我有更多空闲时间，我会去学钢琴。

examples.en: If I were you, I wouldn't lend him any more money.
examples.zh: 如果我是你，我不会再借钱给他。

examples.en: What would you do if you found a wallet in the street?
examples.zh: 如果你在街上捡到一个钱包，你会怎么做？

mastery: 能区分第一条件句（真实可能）和第二条件句（不太可能或想象）。
能把描述现实的句子改写为第二条件句（I don't have a car -> If I had a car, I'd ...）。
能回答和提出假设问题，用第二条件句给出建议。
commonErrors: if 从句用 would：*If I would have money, I would buy it.
主句漏用 would：*If I had time, I go.
汉语“如果”不区分真实与假设，导致该用第二条件句时用第一条件句或反之。
boundaries: 可能发生的真实条件见 kt:en-first-conditional；过去的反事实见 kt:en-third-conditional。
表达愿望 I wish I had ... 见 B2 的 kt:en-wish-present。

primitives.binding: If I had… I would… 与现实有距离 vs 第一条件（c14）；检查 if 从句无 would

kcs.label: 第三条件句：过去的反事实
kcs.description: If + 过去完成时, would have + 过去分词，谈论过去没有发生的情况及其想象中的结果，常用于表达遗憾、庆幸或批评。
forms: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle
could have / might have in the main clause
negative: If I hadn't ..., I wouldn't have ...
contractions: If I'd known, I'd have come. ('d = had / would)

examples.en: If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the train.
examples.zh: 要是我们早点出发，就不会错过火车了。

examples.en: If you'd told me about the party, I would have come.
examples.zh: 如果你早告诉我有聚会，我就来了。

examples.en: She might have won if she hadn't hurt her ankle.
examples.zh: 她要不是扭伤了脚踝，可能就赢了。

mastery: 能从第三条件句中推出实际发生了什么（If I had known -> I didn't know）。
能正确构成两个分句的动词形式，包括缩写 'd。
能对过去的事件表达遗憾或想象不同的结果。
commonErrors: if 从句用 would have：*If I would have known, I would have come.（口语中母语者也说，但标准书面语不接受）
主句漏 have：*I would come if you had told me.（意义变成现在）
误把两个 'd 都理解为同一个词。
boundaries: 跨时间的混合条件句见 kt:en-mixed-conditionals（B2）。
不用 if 表达遗憾的 should have 见 kt:en-past-modals-evaluation。

primitives.binding: 过去反事实 had done/would have done；检查 if 从句无 would have
把实际发生与假设分支放上过去轴

kcs.label: 讲述并评价电影与书
kcs.description: 介绍一部电影或一本书的基本信息和情节，并评价它的优缺点，给出是否推荐的理由。
forms: It's a ... (thriller / comedy / novel) about ...
It's set in ... / It stars ... / It was written by ...
The story is about ... / At the beginning, ... / In the end, ...

kcs.label: 基本被动语态
kcs.description: be + 过去分词构成被动语态，用于动作执行者不重要、未知或显而易见时，把关注点放在受事上。B1 以一般现在时和一般过去时被动为主。
forms: present simple passive: am / is / are + past participle
past simple passive: was / were + past participle
by + agent (only when important)
negative/question: isn't made / Was it built ...?
common uses: made in, built in, written by, invented by, is spoken

examples.en: This bridge was built over two hundred years ago.
examples.zh: 这座桥建于两百多年前。

examples.en: Most of our vegetables are grown locally.
examples.zh: 我们的大部分蔬菜是本地种植的。

examples.en: The novel was written by a sixteen-year-old girl.
examples.zh: 这部小说是一个十六岁的女孩写的。

mastery: 能识别被动句并找出动作的执行者和承受者。
能把主动句转换为一般现在或一般过去被动句，判断是否需要 by 短语。
能在介绍产品、地点或历史时自然使用被动语态。
commonErrors: 漏掉 be：*The bridge built in 1890.
汉语无标记被动（“饭做好了”）导致该用被动时用主动：*The letter sent yesterday.
不及物动词误用被动：*The accident was happened at night.
boundaries: 其他时态、情态被动和 get 被动见 B2 的 kt:en-passive-range；have something done 见 kt:en-causative。
过去分词形式本身见 kt:en-past-participles。

primitives.binding: 从受事视角讲事件：The bridge was built…；检查 be 不漏

kcs.label: 间接引语：陈述句
kcs.description: 转述别人说过的话：用 say / tell 引出，通常把时态往过去推一步，并相应调整人称、指示词和时间地点表达。
forms: said (that) + clause / told + person + (that) + clause
tense backshift: am -> was, will -> would, can -> could, did / have done -> had done
pronoun shift: I -> he / she, my -> his / her
time/place: today -> that day, tomorrow -> the next day, here -> there
no backshift when still true: She said she lives in Rome.

examples.en: Mia said she was too tired to come out.
examples.zh: Mia 说她太累了，不出来了。

examples.en: He told me he had already booked the tickets.
examples.zh: 他告诉我他已经订好票了。

examples.en: The teacher said the test would be on Friday.
examples.zh: 老师说考试在星期五。

mastery: 能把直接引语转换为间接引语，调整时态、代词和时间表达。
能区分 say 与 tell 的句型。
能向第三人转述一段对话的主要内容。
commonErrors: tell 后漏宾语或 say 后加宾语：*He told that ... / *She said me ...
代词不变：*She said I am tired.（意为她自己累）
受汉语影响时态不变化，且在转述明显过去的话时造成歧义。
boundaries: 转述疑问句和命令见 B2 的 kt:en-reported-questions；suggest / promise 等转述动词见 kt:en-reporting-verbs。
时态后移不是绝对规则：内容至今仍真实或刚刚说过时常不后移。

primitives.binding: 引语→转述的时态后移与人称变化推到新句；检查 tell sb/say
say vs tell 按有无宾语选

kcs.label: 间接疑问句（Can you tell me where…?）
kcs.description: 把疑问句嵌入另一句中（Can you tell me ...? / I don't know ...），使提问更礼貌或表达不确定。嵌入部分使用陈述语序，不用 do / does / did 助动词。
forms: Can / Could you tell me + wh-word + subject + verb?
Do you know + wh-word + subject + verb?
I wonder / I'm not sure / I don't know + wh-word + clause
yes/no questions: Do you know if / whether + clause?
Have you any idea how long ...?

examples.en: Could you tell me where the nearest pharmacy is?
examples.zh: 您能告诉我最近的药店在哪儿吗？

examples.en: Do you know if the museum is open on Mondays?
examples.zh: 你知道博物馆星期一开不开门吗？

examples.en: I'm not sure what time the last bus leaves.

mastery: 能识别嵌入问句中的陈述语序。
能把直接问句改写成 Could you tell me ...? / Do you know ...? 形式。
在问路、问服务等场合能主动用间接问句礼貌提问。
commonErrors: 保留疑问语序：*Can you tell me where is the station?
保留助动词：*Do you know what time does the film start?
yes/no 问句漏 if / whether：*Do you know is it open?
boundaries: 转述他人问题（He asked me where I lived）见 B2 的 kt:en-reported-questions。
直接 wh- 问句见 kt:en-wh-questions。

kcs.label: 形容词与副词的形式与角色
kcs.description: 区分形容词与副词的形式和句中角色：形容词修饰名词或作表语（在 be、seem、look 等后），副词修饰动词、形容词或整个句子。重点是 -ly 构成与不规则形式。
forms: adjective + -ly: quick -> quickly, careful -> carefully
spelling: easy -> easily, gentle -> gently, automatic -> automatically
irregular: good -> well, fast -> fast, hard -> hard, late -> late
-ly adjectives (no adverb form): friendly, lovely, lonely -> in a friendly way
linking verbs + adjective: look / sound / smell / feel / seem + adjective
hard vs hardly, late vs lately

examples.en: She speaks English really well, but she writes quite slowly.
examples.zh: 她英语说得很好，但写得比较慢。

examples.en: The soup smells delicious.
examples.zh: 汤闻起来很香。

examples.en: He works hard, but he hardly ever takes a break.
examples.zh: 他工作很努力，但几乎从不休息。

mastery: 能判断句中空位需要形容词还是副词。
能由形容词正确构成副词，包括拼写变化和不规则形式。
描述人和动作时能正确使用形容词与副词，包括感官动词后接形容词。
commonErrors: 受汉语“地”“得”无形式区分影响：*She drives careful. / *He did it good.
感官动词后用副词：*You look nicely.
误解 hardly 为“努力地”：*I studied hardly for the exam.
boundaries: 语义上需要辨别的高阶选择（feel bad / badly）见 B2 的 kt:en-adjective-adverb-choice。
副词的比较级见 kt:en-adverb-comparison；程度副词见 kt:en-adverbs-degree-probability。

primitives.binding: careful vs carefully 修饰名词还是动词；检查 *drives careful
形容词→-ly 副词规则与 good→well

kcs.label: 程度、范围与可能性状语
kcs.term: Adverbial phrases of degree, extent and probability
kcs.description: 用副词或副词短语表达程度、范围和可能性，如 completely、partly、to some extent、definitely、perhaps，使陈述更精确或更有保留。
forms: degree: completely, totally, partly, nearly, almost, hardly, quite, rather
extent phrases: to some extent, in some ways, more or less
probability: definitely, certainly, probably, possibly, perhaps, maybe
position: mid-position (He's probably right) or front (Perhaps he's right)
with negatives: It's not completely true. / I definitely won't ...

examples.en: I completely forgot about the meeting.
examples.zh: 我完全忘了那个会。

examples.en: To some extent, I agree with you, but it's not that simple.
examples.zh: 在某种程度上我同意你，但事情没那么简单。

examples.en: She's almost certainly stuck in traffic.
examples.zh: 她几乎可以肯定是堵在路上了。

mastery: 能按程度或可能性强弱排列一组副词。
能把程度和可能性副词放在句中的正确位置。
表达观点时能用程度副词作出有保留的判断。
commonErrors: 位置错误：*I agree completely with you 可以，但 *I completely am tired 不对（应为 I'm completely tired）。
hardly 后再加否定：*I can't hardly hear you.
maybe 放在助动词后：*It will maybe rain.
boundaries: 表态度的 fortunately / obviously 等见 B2 的 kt:en-attitudinal-adverbs。
情态动词表确定度见 kt:en-certainty-scale；强化词见 kt:en-wide-intensifiers。

primitives.binding: completely/probably 等的位置挪动，看意义与语法（c18）
按程度强弱选副词

kcs.label: 副词的比较级与最高级
kcs.description: 比较两个或多个动作的方式、速度或频率时使用副词的比较级和最高级：短副词加 -er / -est，-ly 副词用 more / most，另有不规则形式。
forms: short adverbs: faster, harder, earlier, later (the) fastest
-ly adverbs: more carefully, (the) most slowly
irregular: well -> better -> best, badly -> worse -> worst, far -> further / farther
as + adverb + as: as quickly as possible
less + adverb: less often

examples.en: Could you speak a bit more slowly, please?
examples.zh: 请您说慢一点好吗？

examples.en: Of all the players, Sam played the best.
examples.zh: 在所有选手中，Sam 发挥得最好。

examples.en: We'll need to leave earlier than usual tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我们明天得比平时早出发。

mastery: 能写出常见副词的比较级和最高级，包括不规则形式。
能区分形容词比较级与副词比较级的使用位置。
能比较人们做事的方式（谁跑得更快、谁说得更清楚）。
commonErrors: -ly 副词加 -er：*quicklier / *carefullier。
用形容词比较级修饰动词：*She sings more beautiful than me.
*more better / *gooder。
boundaries: 形容词比较级与最高级见 kt:en-comparatives、kt:en-superlatives。
quick / quickly 等形容词与副词的基本区分见 kt:en-adjectives-adverbs。

primitives.binding: more carefully/faster/better 规则推到新副词；检查 *quicklier
比较图中两人动作快慢

kcs.label: too / enough / so 与结果限制
kcs.description: too 表示“过于”，超出所需或可接受的程度，常带否定结果；enough 表示“足够”；so / such 表示程度高并可引出结果从句。
forms: too + adjective/adverb (+ for someone) (+ to-infinitive): too hot to drink
too much / too many + noun
adjective/adverb + enough (+ to-infinitive): old enough to vote
enough + noun: enough time / money

examples.en: The tea is too hot to drink right now.
examples.zh: 茶现在太烫了，没法喝。

examples.en: Are you old enough to drive?
examples.zh: 你到年龄可以开车了吗？

examples.en: There isn't enough milk for everyone.
examples.zh: 牛奶不够每个人喝。

mastery: 能区分 too（过度、负面）与 very（程度高）的意义。
能把 enough 放在形容词后、名词前的正确位置。
能用 too / enough + to-infinitive 解释某事为什么能或不能做。
commonErrors: 用 too 表示“非常”的正面意思：*The food is too delicious!（口语夸张除外）
enough 位置错误：*enough old / *money enough（后者古旧）。
too ... to 句中多余宾语：*The box is too heavy to carry it.
boundaries: much too / far too 等进一步强化见 kt:en-wide-intensifiers。
so 作结果连词见 kt:en-because-so。
so / such … that 表程度与结果见 kt:en-so-such。

primitives.binding: enough—very—too 程度定位，too 带负面结果；检查 *too delicious
too heavy to carry 判断能否做到
